(b) Construction/reproducibility risk (Scorer B's central concern, echoed by both scorers' low implementationTrialTractability scores of 4 and 3): the trap depends on two timing-sensitive, environment-fragile events -- landing a read inside the replication lag window and reliably triggering a VACUUM-induced recovery-conflict cancellation -- known to be sensitive to hardware, container scheduling, WAL volume, and max_standby_streaming_delay tuning; if these can't be forced deterministically across every trial and environment, verifier outcomes will partly reflect infra nondeterminism rather than agent reasoning. Risk (a) threatens the family's value even if built perfectly; risk (b) threatens whether it can be built reproducibly at all -- both should be probed (see cheapestFalsifyingProbe) before committing full build hours.
reconciled.semanticOverlapGroup: stale-authoritative-state-reconciliation / stale-replica-authority-consistency: an instance of "agent holds a cached, lagged, or non-authoritative view of state/authority and must reconcile against current true state rather than trusting the stale view," shared with this portfolio's deployment-model-alias-rollout-drift, model-alias-drift-sentinel, delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation, stale-crm-ticket-automation, caa-revalidation, and the retry-budget-carryover (failover-to-replica) candidate. This is the first instance grounded specifically in live Postgres physical streaming replication and recovery-conflict semantics rather than failover, caching, or alias-rollout semantics -- a materially distinct concrete mechanism within an already well-populated conceptual family, which tempers its noveltyPortfolioContribution score.
reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
opportunityScoreTotal: A=69 vs B=71 (delta=2, within the 10-point tolerance) -- essentially consensus, with every per-dimension gap at most 1 point (economicValue 7/8, naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace 9/10, subjectInaccessibleAuthority 6/7, constructionOperatorCompatibility 7/6, implementationTrialTractability 4/3, noveltyPortfolioContribution 3/4). No explicit-delta justification is strictly triggered by the rule here, so I averaged per-dimension and, for the six half-integer ties, split rounding direction 3-up/3-down based on each scorer's own stated reasoning rather than arbitrarily: rounded up economicValue and naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace (crediting the five explicit natural-scenario dimensions and real production-incident cost), rounded down constructionOperatorCompatibility and implementationTrialTractability (both scorers independently flag real Docker/replication-harness build friction), and rounded down subjectInaccessibleAuthority / up noveltyPortfolioContribution to keep the sum exact. Result: final total of 70, the arithmetic midpoint, not a cherry-picked endpoint.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage and probabilityFullRecipe: this DOES trigger the >15pp rule at face value (raw gaps of ~49.6 and ~19.85 points), but the trigger is a unit-scale bug, not a substantive disagreement, and must not be papered over by blind averaging. Scorer A reports probabilityOrdinaryPackage=50 (range 35-65) and probabilityFullRecipe=20 (range 10-30) on an implicit 0-100 percentage-point scale -- yet Scorer A's own officialReviewProbability (0.45) and tenDistinctTaskProbability (0.6) use a 0-1 fraction scale, an internal inconsistency within Scorer A's own output. Scorer B instead uses 0-1 fractions consistently across all four probability fields (0.40/0.15/0.35/0.6), which is the self-consistent convention. Rescaling Scorer A's two affected values by /100 (0.50 and 0.20) to match the shared fraction convention shows the TRUE disagreement is only 10 percentage points on probabilityOrdinaryPackage (0.50 vs 0.40) and 5 points on probabilityFullRecipe (0.20 vs 0.15) -- both comfortably under the 15pp threshold once correctly scaled. A literal blind average of the raw, mismatched-scale numbers (e.g. (50+0.4)/2=25.2, or (20+0.15)/2=10.075) would be a meaningless artifact of unit confusion, not a real belief about pass probability. Final values instead average the two unit-corrected estimates -- probabilityOrdinaryPackage=0.45 (range 0.30-0.60), probabilityFullRecipe=0.17 (range 0.08-0.28), both medium confidence -- which sit almost exactly at the midpoint of the corrected estimates, favoring neither the higher (more building-friendly) nor the lower (more 'diagnostically hard') reading.

Secondary fields: officialReviewProbability averaged to 0.40 (0.45 vs 0.35, a 10pp gap, under threshold); tenDistinctTaskProbability unchanged at 0.6 (exact agreement); firstPackageBuildHours averaged to 34 (32 vs 36); marginalBuildHours averaged to 6.5 (5 vs 8). cheapestFalsifyingProbe and principalValidityRisk were merged rather than taken from one scorer: Scorer B's infra-only reproducibility probe is logically prior to and cheaper than Scorer A's agent-in-the-loop probe (both scorers independently scored implementationTrialTractability low, 4 and 3, flagging real build risk), so the reconciled probe sequences B's infra check first and A's agent-behavior check second. principalValidityRisk merges both scorers' concerns as two distinct, both-must-be-resolved risks: (a) training-data contamination suppressing diagnostic yield (Scorer A's concern, and the dominant one given both scorers' own strongestReasonWrong sections argue the full-recipe pass rate could run even higher than estimated) and (b) timing/infra nondeterminism threatening reproducible construction (Scorer B's concern). Net effect of this reconciliation is neutral, not flattering: the final opportunityScoreTotal (70) and probabilityFullRecipe (0.17) sit at true midpoints of the corrected inputs, neither inflated toward a more attractive-looking family nor deflated toward a more 'diagnostically hard'-looking one.

family.name: Ambiguous-Failure Payment Retry Discipline
family.definition: Agent issues a payment action where the network call can fail after the server-side effect has partially or fully completed; correct behavior reuses the same idempotency key or re-queries ledger state before resubmitting, and correctly treats a concurrent-conflict response as retry-safe rather than rotating keys and double-charging.
family.taskShape: Harness injects timeouts at ambiguous completion points, sometimes racing a concurrent duplicate submission under the same key; agent must choose retry-with-same-key vs. query-then-decide vs. legitimate-new-key across several such events in one workflow.
family.authorityBoundary: Agent is authorized to charge exactly once per logical intent; key reuse is valid only for identical intent, and the ledger, not client belief, is ground truth.
family.subjectInaccessibleWitness: Whether the original attempt completed server-side before the client-visible failure is not observable except by querying ledger state.
family.naturalScenarioDimensions: failure point relative to commit; presence of a genuine parameter change requiring a new key; concurrent same-key race vs sequential retry; workflow chain length.
family.whyAgentMayFail: A naive agent treats an errored call as a no-op and blindly retries or rotates keys, producing a real duplicate charge invisible in any single response.
family.whyFair: Idempotency-key discipline is standard, published professional practice (e.g. Stripe API design guidance); the task applies a known, derivable rule under realistic ambiguity.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage.rationale: Normalized both scorers to a 0-1 fraction (A reported 35 on an implicit 0-100 scale; B reported 0.5 on an explicit 0-1 scale -- these are the same units meaning 35% vs 50%, a 15pp gap sitting right at the reconciliation threshold). I weight toward A's lower figure because it is corroborated by in-repo evidence B did not use: this family's causal axis (duplicate-side-effects / uncertain-external-effects) was already built and run end-to-end as the durable-approval-outbox project, and all six frontier trials (cc267-claude-1/2/3, cc267-codex-1/2/3) show non-trivial failure -- 2 to 13 of 24 scenarios failing per trial, mostly on audit_explains/completion checks (see trials/durable-approval-outbox/*/result.json). That is direct evidence that frontier agents do NOT cleanly ace this failure family by rule-recall alone, which argues against B's higher estimate. I did not push all the way to A's point value because B's core argument -- that 'query-then-decide' is simultaneously the textbook-correct move and a universally-safe default, so an ordinarily-built (unhardened) package may let agents pass via a safe default without real diagnosis -- is independently valid and not addressed by the outbox evidence, which was a harder, more hardened construction than a first-cut ordinary package would be.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.evidenceUsed: Normalized units from both scorers; trials/durable-approval-outbox/*/result.json failure counts; data/mechanisms.json entries for duplicate-side-effects and uncertain-external-effects; data/candidate-pool.json entry for payment-unknown-capture-receipt.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.strongestReasonWrong: durable-approval-outbox is a materially different, more complex task shape (multi-step outbox/approval workflow) than a first-cut 'ordinary package' of this family would be, so its failure rate may understate how easy an unhardened version of THIS family actually is; the true ordinary-package rate could sit closer to B's 0.5 if the initial build is simple.

probabilityFullRecipe.rationale: After normalizing units (A: 15% -> 0.15; B: 20% -> 0.20), the two estimates are only 5pp apart -- well under the 15pp reconciliation threshold -- and their reasoning is essentially convergent: both expect a fully hardened recipe to strip surface cues, tighten the concurrent-race window, add genuine-new-key traps, and lengthen the chain, each additional hardened decision point multiplying the chance of at least one wrong call. A straightforward average (0.175, rounded to 0.17) is appropriate here since neither the magnitude of the gap nor the underlying rationale conflicts.
probabilityFullRecipe.evidenceUsed: Both scorers' convergent reasoning about compounding per-event failure probability across a hardened multi-event chain; the taskShape's own naturalScenarioDimensions.
probabilityFullRecipe.strongestReasonWrong: If the domain's correct policy really does collapse to a small, well-internalized decision procedure (reuse key unless intent changed, else query ledger), even adversarially hardened instances might still be resolved correctly at a materially higher rate than either scorer estimates.

reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
Two things crossed the mandatory-justification thresholds: opportunityScoreTotal differs by 11 points (69 vs 80, >10), and probabilityOrdinaryPackage differs by 15pp once normalized to common units (35% vs 50%, at the boundary but close enough to warrant explicit treatment given the units mismatch itself is a red flag worth surfacing).

Three concrete findings drove the reconciliation rather than a blind average:

1. Scorer B's latentDiagnosisReasoningBurden=12 is an out-of-range value. Every other sub-score either scorer produced across the whole breakdown tops out at 10 (both hit naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace=10 as an apparent ceiling), so 12 looks like a rubric violation or a slip rather than a deliberately wider scale. I capped it to 10 before averaging with A's 8, landing on 9 -- this alone explains roughly a third of the 11-point total gap and is not a real signal that should inflate the family's score.

2. Scorer A's noveltyPortfolioContribution=1 vs Scorer B's =3 is the second-largest driver of the total-score gap, and I verified A's underlying claim directly against repo state rather than trusting either scorer's assertion: data/candidate-pool.json's `payment-unknown-capture-receipt` entry lists failureMechanisms exactly `["uncertain-external-effects","duplicate-side-effects","false-audit-history"]` -- the same two mechanisms this family's causalAxis centers on, in the same payments domain, built on the same core hypothesis (an ambiguous completion collapses into a wrong decision before ground truth answers). That candidate is already reports/discovery-workbench-report.md-flagged task-shape-ready, and the same two mechanisms were already exercised end-to-end via the durable-approval-outbox project (six trials, all showing real failure, per trials/durable-approval-outbox/*/result.json). Scorer B's own text explicitly says it used "Family definition only (no mutant/mechanism/contract data used)" -- so B could not have discovered this concrete overlap and its higher novelty score is the less-informed of the two. I weighted the reconciled noveltyPortfolioContribution to A's value (1), not an average, because A's number is verified against artifacts and B's is not.

3. Both scorers independently converge on the same principal risk in different words -- A frames it as precedented overlap/killed-candidate risk, B frames it as shortcut-collapse via the textbook-safe "always query ledger first" default -- which is mutually reinforcing, not contradictory. That convergence, plus (1) and (2) above, is why verifierAntiCheatFeasibility and materiallyDistinctInstanceCapacity were reconciled toward the more conservative of the two raw scores rather than averaged: a family this close to an already-built, already-partially-failing sibling candidate has a narrower true anti-cheat margin and a smaller pool of genuinely distinct hardened instances than either scorer's number alone implies. Net effect: final opportunityScoreTotal (71) sits much closer to A's 69 than to B's 80, and this is a deliberate, evidence-backed pull toward the more skeptical, better-grounded estimate -- not a rounding artifact and not an attempt to flatter either score.

One correction to Scorer A's own report for the record: A's principalValidityRisk cites "six frontier trials at reward 0" for durable-approval-outbox; the actual result.json files carry `reward: null` (not present/zero) and instead report scenario-level failure counts (2-13 of 24 scenarios failing per trial). The substance of A's claim -- persistent, non-trivial agent failure on this mechanism pair, already measured in this repo -- holds up under inspection, but the literal "reward 0" phrasing is not what the artifacts show, so I did not import that specific number into the reconciled analysis.
reconciled.cheapestFalsifyingProbe: Merge of both scorers' proposals, which were substantively identical: script a static, non-reasoning procedure -- "always re-query ledger/settlement state before any resubmission; reuse the same idempotency key unless a request parameter literally changed" -- and run it against the verifier across every scored event in a candidate instance. Additionally diff its pass pattern against the existing payment-unknown-capture-receipt probe harness (data/spec-probe-payment-unknown-capture.json) which already exercises the same two mechanisms. If the naive static rule clears 5/6+ scored events, or if this family's probe results pattern-match the already-run payment-unknown-capture-receipt probe outcomes, the family is not adding discriminating signal beyond either rule-following or an already-measured mechanism, and should not consume further build hours before that gap is addressed.
reconciled.principalValidityRisk: Two compounding, verified risks. First, precedent/overlap: this family's causal axis (duplicate-side-effects, uncertain-external-effects) is not a fresh mechanism for this repo -- it is already registered in data/mechanisms.json and already built and run as both payment-unknown-capture-receipt (task-shape-ready, same domain, same failureMechanisms, per data/candidate-pool.json) and durable-approval-outbox (six trials run, all showing real failure, per trials/durable-approval-outbox/*/result.json). A candidate this close to already-measured work risks contributing little beyond what's already evidenced, and the "killed on a bounded settlement window" failure mode documented for the durable-approval-outbox lineage is a directly analogous construction trap here. Second, shortcut-collapse: idempotency-key discipline (same key on retry, query ledger when ambiguous) is one of the most heavily published patterns in backend/payments engineering (Stripe's own docs), and the always-safe fallback (query-then-decide) is also the textbook-correct move in most described scenarios -- so an unhardened package risks eliciting correct behavior via memorized declarative recall or a universally-safe default rather than genuine per-event ledger diagnosis, inflating apparent pass rates under both ordinary and moderately hardened builds unless the recipe specifically engineers cases where that default is insufficient or costly.
reconciled.semanticOverlapGroup: payments duplicate-side-effects / uncertain-external-effects cluster (retry-duplicate-side-effect-under-ambiguous-network-failure) -- verified near-duplicate of the existing candidate-pool entry payment-unknown-capture-receipt (identical failureMechanisms list, same domain, same "ambiguous completion resolves only via authoritative ledger" hypothesis) and direct overlap with the two mechanisms already registered in data/mechanisms.json and already measured end-to-end via this repo's durable-approval-outbox project.

family.name: Worker Rebalance Callback Deduplication
family.definition: A stateful worker process must keep exactly-bounded, non-duplicated external side effects (e.g. customer notifications) correct when it crashes, restarts, and transiently overlaps ownership with another worker instance during a consumer-group/partition rebalance.
family.taskShape: Agent operates a live event-consumer service; the harness kills/restarts workers and forces partition-ownership overlap under continuous traffic; the agent must sequence state-commit vs. offset-commit vs. external-callback so kill/restart/scale sequences never silently drop or double-fire a customer-visible effect, within a documented duplicate tolerance.
family.authorityBoundary: A worker's claim to a partition/consumer-group slot is time-bounded and revocable by the group coordinator; only the currently-owning worker may emit the callback for a given event.
family.subjectInaccessibleWitness: Exact rebalance-protocol state and kill/restart timing are controlled by the harness and not introspectable by the agent in advance.
family.naturalScenarioDimensions: worker restart timing; overlap window length; traffic rate; duplicate-tolerance threshold; number of concurrent worker slots.
family.whyAgentMayFail: Agents commonly order offset-commit before or after the external call incorrectly, or assume single-worker exclusivity, producing lost or duplicated callbacks under overlap.
family.whyFair: The commit-then-emit-then-ack ordering discipline is standard, documented distributed-systems practice (Kafka consumer-group semantics) requiring genuine reasoning, and a tolerance band keeps the check achievable rather than trivia-hard.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage.rationale: Normalized to a common percentage scale, A (30%, range 20-40) and B (35% from 0.35, range 25-45) are only 5pp apart -- well under the 15pp reconciliation threshold -- and corroborate rather than conflict. Both independently land on the same qualitative call via different routes: A grounds it in the in-portfolio 'duplicate-side-effects' mechanism's documented failure mode (agents pick a delivery-id/UUID key instead of a durable-identity key) stacked with a second, less-internalized fencing/generation-number discipline; B reasons from the family definition's own whyAgentMayFail text describing the same two failure surfaces. Both also name the identical upside risk (a generous duplicate-tolerance band letting a naive shim pass by luck). A convergent average is appropriate rather than picking either single value.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.evidenceUsed: Verified A's cited 'duplicate-side-effects' mechanism entry against data/mechanisms.json (id: duplicate-side-effects, maturity: measured, tied to the durable-approval-outbox family) -- confirmed it exists with the described key-instability failure mode. B used only the family definition text, no repo evidence.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.strongestReasonWrong: If the harness's forced-overlap window is rare/short relative to trial length or the tolerance band is generous, a boilerplate 'idempotency key + at-least-once retry' shim could clear most trials without any fencing-specific reasoning, pushing the true rate above 45% -- a risk both scorers explicitly name.

probabilityFullRecipe.rationale: Normalized, A=60% and B=80% -- a 20pp gap exceeding the 15pp reconciliation threshold, so this required verification rather than averaging. Checking A's citations against data/hardness-operators.json: the 'verifier-process-and-ledger-isolation' operator's 113/113-to-267/267 figures, which A partly leans on for 'moving toward a much higher clean-solve rate,' are explicitly logged in-repo as verifier-bypass artifacts, not agent solve rates ('the old perfect scores were verifier bypasses... must not be credited as hardness') -- so part of A's own evidence is a validity fix, not a hardness data point, and A's prose overstates it. The one real measured hardness effect in that citation pair, 'a2-explicit-terminal-state-repair' (a full, deliberate, correct fix for a comparable exactly-once/terminal-state family), moved clean-solve rate from only 2/6 (33%) to 3/6 (50%) -- a real but modest gain, well below B's 70-90% range and even below the midpoint of A's own 45-70% range. A second, more directly analogous operator neither scorer cited, 'committed-idempotency-authority' (persisting a committed idempotency key across lease/generation epochs -- precisely this family's fencing mechanic), returned a null/inconclusive Phase 14 result (8/8 in both treatment and control arms; 'no positive effect established... no root-cause labels ran'), so the repo's closest empirical analog neither confirms nor refutes a high ceiling. B's 70-90% is a first-principles 'narrow, well-understood fix space' prior explicitly built on 'no measured pass-rate data,' and does not engage this record at all. Weighing the (partially misapplied, but real) empirical anchor toward a moderate ceiling against the legitimate point that a genuinely complete two-part recipe (committed key + fencing token + strict commit-then-emit-then-ack, addressing both failure surfaces at once) should outperform a single-axis wording fix, the reconciled estimate sits closer to A, nudged upward, carrying wide uncertainty forward as low confidence.
probabilityFullRecipe.evidenceUsed: data/hardness-operators.json -- verified 'verifier-process-and-ledger-isolation' (bypass repair, not a hardness measurement), 'a2-explicit-terminal-state-repair' (2/6->3/6 measured), and 'committed-idempotency-authority' (8/8 both arms, inconclusive) directly against the repo; data/mechanisms.json 'duplicate-side-effects' entry for sibling-mechanism context.
probabilityFullRecipe.strongestReasonWrong: The a2 and committed-idempotency-authority analogs come from a different family (durable-approval-outbox) under different, narrower interventions (a one-sentence spec clarification; an epoch-key recovery patch), not literally 'the full documented recipe' for this family's dual-ownership/fencing wrinkle -- if this family's harness has a more generous tolerance band or less adversarial timing than its sibling, the true ceiling could legitimately sit closer to B's 80-90%, as B argues.

reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
Three quantities crossed or approached the mandatory-justification bar; none were resolved by blind averaging.

(1) opportunityScoreTotal: A=59 vs B=67, Δ8 -- under the 10-point threshold, but the two largest per-dimension gaps are independently resolvable against the repo, so I reconciled dimension-by-dimension rather than averaging the totals (which would have given 63). authoritativeProvenance (3 vs 6): the family's primarySourceUnitIds ('tb-repo-root', 'tb-merged-tasks-sample') are generic internal-looking identifiers, not a named, checkable authoritative external source despite evidenceType='fresh-external' -- sided with A's skepticism (set 4). noveltyPortfolioContribution (1 vs 3): verified against data/mechanisms.json that a 'duplicate-side-effects' mechanism (maturity: measured) already exists in-portfolio, tied to the durable-approval-outbox family -- this new family is a close, low-novelty sibling, though the dual-ownership/fencing wrinkle is a genuine (if modest) increment, so set 2, near A but not zero. verifierAntiCheatFeasibility (6 vs 8): B's 8 is internally inconsistent with B's own principalValidityRisk text, which flags harness-timing nondeterminism as complicating 'reproducible grading' -- combined with A's concrete citation of three historical verifier bypasses for this exact mechanism class (data/mechanisms.json cheatRisks), this favors A's more cautious 6. constructionOperatorCompatibility (8 vs 5): split toward B's lower estimate (6), since both scorers' agreement on implementationTrialTractability=3 and firstPackageBuildHours=40 (heavy bespoke chaos-harness construction) is hard to square with A's high compatibility score. Remaining dimensions had gaps ≤2 and were averaged directly. Reconciled total: 60 -- close to A, not a flattering pick toward either input, and driven by verifiable repo evidence rather than a coin-flip average.

(2) probabilityOrdinaryPackage: after normalizing units (A already in percentage points: 30%; B in decimal: 0.35 = 35%), the gap is 5pp, under the 15pp threshold -- straightforward convergent average to 32%, both lines of reasoning corroborating.

(3) probabilityFullRecipe: normalized, A=60% vs B=80%, a 20pp gap exceeding the 15pp threshold -- mandatory explicit reconciliation performed above. In short: A's own supporting citation partly conflates a verifier-bypass repair (not a real hardness measurement) with a real but modest hardness result (2/6->3/6, i.e. ~50%, for a comparable full deliberate fix in a sibling family); B's higher estimate rests on an admitted zero-evidence prior and ignores both that modest analog and a more directly on-point but inconclusive null-result operator (committed-idempotency-authority, 8/8 both arms) that neither scorer used. Final reconciled value: 62% (range 45-78, confidence downgraded to low to reflect the genuine, only-partially-resolvable disagreement) -- closer to A but nudged up for the legitimate 'complete recipe beats a single-axis wording fix' argument, and explicitly short of B's 80-90% ceiling, which the evidence does not support.

(4) officialReviewProbability (0.25 vs 0.4) and tenDistinctTaskProbability (0.45 vs 0.6) each show exactly a 15pp gap -- at, not over, the threshold -- so these were averaged directly (0.32 and 0.52) without a mandatory-justification writeup; both scorers offer only decision-prior reasoning with no repo grounding on these two fields specifically.

No result here was chosen to look favorable: the reconciled opportunityScoreTotal (60) and probabilityFullRecipe (62%) both land below the higher of the two independent inputs, tracking where the verified evidence actually points.
reconciled.cheapestFalsifyingProbe: Stand up a minimal 2-worker consumer-group harness (e.g. kafka-python or testcontainers) with a mock callback endpoint logging every invocation by event id. Under the harness's actual (not idealized) kill/restart and rebalance-overlap injection at the documented duplicate-tolerance threshold, run two variants back to back: (1) a naive at-least-once + in-memory/persisted dedup-by-event-id shim with no commit-order discipline and no generation/epoch fencing, and (2) the deliberate commit-then-emit-then-ack ordering with a durably committed key and fencing token. If (1) already clears 5/6-6/6 trials, the family's claimed reasoning burden is inflated and it reduces to a boilerplate pattern (falsifying the difficulty claim); if the forced overlap/kill sequence does not reliably produce an observable duplicate-or-drop for the wrong ordering while (2) stays clean, the family's premise that the harness naturally and repeatably exposes this failure is falsified before further construction investment.
reconciled.principalValidityRisk: Two compounding, evidence-grounded risks. First, harness/verifier timing nondeterminism: kill signals, forced-rebalance triggers, and live traffic race each other, so pass/fail can hinge on incidental timing luck rather than the agent's commit/callback ordering discipline -- this repo's own 'duplicate-side-effects' mechanism entry documents the identical risk class for a sibling family (a bounded external dedup window punishing correct late reconciliation) plus three concrete historical verifier bypasses (trivial never-execute, ledger-rebinding, self-report counting) that a naive verifier for this new family would likely reproduce absent a deliberately isolated, floor-and-ceiling external ledger. Second, task collapse: the commit-order discipline is a well-documented pattern (idempotency keys / outbox), so the task may reduce to 'apply the standard recipe' rather than requiring the claimed fencing-specific reasoning, especially if the duplicate-tolerance band is generous -- undermining both the difficulty claim and the verifier anti-cheat feasibility score simultaneously.
reconciled.semanticOverlapGroup: duplicate-side-effects / exactly-once-retry-idempotency (direct sibling of the in-portfolio 'duplicate-side-effects' mechanism, maturity: measured, tied to the durable-approval-outbox family; distinguishing wrinkle is transient dual-partition-ownership/fencing across rebalance generations rather than single-process crash-retry alone)

family.name: Rollback That Reactivates a Dormant Defect
family.definition: Responding to a live incident on one of several replicated deployment targets, the agent must diagnose root cause before acting, because rolling back a recent change without isolating the cause can reproduce an identical latent bug -- a repurposed flag/identifier reaching never-removed deprecated code -- on previously-unaffected replicas.
family.taskShape: Multiple identical replicas exist; one exhibits a defect traced to a reused identifier reactivating deprecated code; a plausible fast fix (rollback everywhere) is deliberately available as a trap, and the agent must audit per-replica deployment history/reachable code before broadly remediating.
family.authorityBoundary: Agent has standing fleet deploy/rollback authority, but exercising it without verifying uniform pre-incident state across replicas exceeds the safe scope of a 'simple' rollback; each replica is independently authoritative for its own runtime state.
family.subjectInaccessibleWitness: Dormant legacy code gated by a repurposed flag is not visible from the current deployment manifest or diff alone; it requires inspecting actual reachable runtime code paths per replica.
family.naturalScenarioDimensions: number of replicas; which is affected first; remediation options offered; presence of a written double-check deployment procedure.
family.whyAgentMayFail: Under incident time pressure, 'roll back everywhere' is the obvious action, so an agent applying it reflexively reproduces the identical failure on every remaining healthy replica -- the real Knight Capital escalation.
family.whyFair: Drawn from a public, regulator-documented (SEC) incident; the reasoning required -- verify per-node deployment state before broad remediation -- is standard incident-response discipline, not proprietary or obscure.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage.rationale: Once Scorer B's 0-1 fractional value (0.4, range 0.3-0.5) is converted to the same percentage-point basis Scorer A used (45, range 30-60), the two are in real agreement (40 vs 45, 5pp apart) -- this is not a substantive disagreement, just a units-convention mismatch in the raw inputs. Both scorers independently converge on 'a bit above a coin flip': the generic 'investigate before broad remediation' heuristic is well-primed in frontier agents, but genuine per-replica code-reachability diagnosis of the specific reused-identifier mechanism is a materially higher bar than generic caution, and an unhardened package could tip either way depending on how visibly the anomalous replica is flagged versus how well the deprecated-code evidence is exposed through the starter's tools.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.evidenceUsed: Scorer A's rationale (frontier-agent incident-response caution norms; this repo's pattern of several deployment/rollback-shaped families turning out low-difficulty once built) and Scorer B's rationale (rollback-everywhere as a documented reflexive agentic shortcut under incident-style time pressure), reconciled after normalizing B's 0-1 scale to percentage points.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.strongestReasonWrong: If the ordinary package makes the bad replica trivially distinguishable via an obvious manifest/diff tell, or conversely buries the deprecated-code evidence behind a tool call the starter doesn't surface, the true rate could land well outside this band in either direction -- exactly the concern both scorers raised independently.

probabilityFullRecipe.rationale: After normalizing units (Scorer B's 0.2/[0.1,0.3] is a fractional-scale value equivalent to 20%/[10,30] on Scorer A's percentage-point scale), the two estimates are 65% vs 20% -- a genuine 45-point disagreement, not a units artifact, about which *direction* full-recipe hardening pushes this family's pass rate. Scorer A argues hardening mainly strips spurious noise (ambiguous specs, poorly-exposed evidence) that would otherwise unfairly fail capable agents, revealing a near-ceiling true capability -- and backs this with concrete same-repo evidence: Phase 14 measured deployment-rollback-recompute, a full-recipe-built, concentrated-scenario, verifier-hardened sibling family in the identical 'deployment rollback' domain, at 2/2 clean solves (OpenAI + Anthropic) with confirmed verifier discrimination (18/18 narrow-mutant catches, 0/6 false positives on controls) -- i.e., hardening did NOT suppress the rate for the closest available comparable. Scorer B argues hardening mainly strips cheap shortcuts (generic caution boilerplate, memorized Knight Capital recall) that inflate an unhardened rate, but explicitly labels this 'qualitative extrapolation... not a numeric derivation from any mutant, mechanism, or reward count' for this or any measured analog -- it is unfalsified assertion, not evidence. On the other hand, B's concern is not weightless: this family carries a contamination risk the Phase 14 comparable did not -- Knight Capital is an unusually famous, SEC-documented, publicly named incident (named explicitly in the family's own 'whyFair' field), materially raising the odds that a well-built anti-cheat verifier is specifically engineered to defeat pattern-matched recall rather than reward it, which could suppress the rate below the Phase 14 precedent. Both scorers' own 'strongestReasonWrong' entries concede the other's point (A concedes real diagnostic difficulty could hold the rate down; B concedes the single-flag/single-branch mechanism is not deeply combinatorial once an agent decides to look), which is itself evidence that neither 65 nor 20 should stand unmodified. Net: repo-grounded precedent plus the non-combinatorial mechanism argue against B's low estimate, but the family's unusually high-profile contamination risk argues against A's near-ceiling estimate. 45%, well below A and well above B, with wide bounds and low confidence, is the defensible synthesis pending the falsifying probe below.
probabilityFullRecipe.evidenceUsed: reports/PHASE-14-OPERATOR-EFFECTS.md: deployment-rollback-recompute measured at 2/2 COUNTED_SOLVE (0/2 reward-zero) under the full construction recipe (concentrated-24 scenario selection, seeded-recompute starter), with local reference/mutant calibration confirming verifier discrimination (18/18 narrow-target, 0/6 narrow-control) -- the only direct same-repo, same-domain, full-recipe empirical data point bearing on this question; both scorers' rationale/strongestReasonWrong text.
probabilityFullRecipe.strongestReasonWrong: The Phase 14 comparable's mechanism (uncertain-external-effects/duplicate-side-effects idempotent recompute) is causally different from this family's reused-identifier/dormant-code diagnostic mechanism, and it carries no equivalent famous-incident contamination risk -- so it may simply be the wrong reference class, and the true rate could sit much closer to either scorer's original number than this synthesis assumes.

reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
Two distinct issues surfaced, and they needed to be handled separately rather than blindly averaged.

(1) opportunityScoreTotal (72 vs 75, delta 3) is within the 10-point tolerance and reflects real, narrow agreement -- both scorers gave identical or near-identical marks on 7 of 10 axes, including the two most consequential (latentDiagnosisReasoningBurden: 11/11, authoritativeProvenance: 9/9). The final breakdown does not simply average every axis: it keeps noveltyPortfolioContribution at B's lower value (2, not the midpoint 2.5) because a repo search confirms B's specific overlap claim -- 'deployment-rollback-partial-effects' is a real, still-open candidate familyId already tracked across this project's phase-15/16 reader packets and novelty-baseline data, and this family would directly compete for that slot alongside two already-built siblings (deployment-rollback-recompute, deployment-model-alias-rollout-drift) in the same domain. That is a verified, not speculative, novelty drag, so it should not be diluted by averaging with A's less-informed 3. The other axes were set at or near A's original values (siding with A where the two were within 1 point) since B's slightly higher marks on economicValue/naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace/constructionOperatorCompatibility were not independently justified beyond generic optimism. Net total: 71.

(2) probabilityFullRecipe is the real flag. Scorer A reports probabilityOrdinaryPackage/probabilityFullRecipe on a 0-100 percentage-point scale (45, 65) while Scorer B reports the identical fields on a 0-1 fractional scale (0.4, 0.2) -- confirmed by B's internally consistent use of 0-1 across officialReviewProbability and tenDistinctTaskProbability too, and by the reconciliation instructions' own 'percentage points' framing, which matches A's convention. Converting B to percentage points (40%, 20%) shows probabilityOrdinaryPackage was never really in dispute (40 vs 45, 5pp) -- but probabilityFullRecipe was: 65% vs 20%, a 45-point gap, well past the 15pp bar for mandatory justification. This is a substantive disagreement about the *direction* hardening moves the pass rate (A: up, toward a noise-free ceiling, evidenced by a directly comparable Phase 14 full-recipe family scoring 2/2 clean; B: down, toward suppressing memorized-recall/generic-caution shortcuts, evidenced only by unverified qualitative extrapolation that B itself flags as non-empirical). I weighted the repo-grounded precedent over the unfalsified extrapolation but did not adopt A's number outright, because this family's contamination exposure (a uniquely famous, named, SEC-documented incident) is qualitatively worse than the Phase 14 comparable's and is a legitimate, independently-raised reason a properly hardened verifier could underperform that precedent. Final: 45% (range 25-65, confidence lowered to 'low' for both scorers on this field), explicitly not a flattering pick toward either side, with the cheapest-falsifying-probe recommendation given priority before further build investment. officialReviewProbability (0.40 vs 0.55, 15pp) sits at the stated boundary rather than over it; reconciled to 0.48 by light averaging since neither scorer offered a differentiated causal argument for their number, unlike the FullRecipe case. tenDistinctTaskProbability (0.6 vs 0.65) and firstPackageBuildHours (32/32) needed no reconciliation; marginalBuildHours (6 vs 8) was averaged to 7 for the same reason as officialReviewProbability. A process note for the scoring pipeline: pin down a single probability scale (0-100 vs 0-1) in the scorer prompt template -- this mismatch could silently distort automated reconciliation if not caught by a human/LLM reviewer normalizing units before diffing.
reconciled.cheapestFalsifyingProbe: Before building the full fleet/replica harness, draft only the scenario manifest plus a verifier stub and a minimal 2-replica instance (one broken via the reused-flag/deprecated-code mechanism, one healthy), and run one blind frontier-agent probe with no scaffolding hints. Check whether a response that only expresses generic incident-response caution ("investigate before touching other replicas") or a memorized "this is like Knight Capital" recall -- without ever inspecting per-replica reachable code or naming the reused-identifier mechanism -- is scoreable as a pass by the verifier, and separately whether it in fact avoids reactivating the dormant defect. If generic caution alone clears the verifier, or if a trivial 100%-catch/100%-fail split appears with no real per-replica evidence-gathering in the transcript, the family's core value proposition is falsified cheaply, before any scenario-space or verifier build-out -- and this result would also directly adjudicate the 65%-vs-20% probabilityFullRecipe dispute between the two scorers.
reconciled.principalValidityRisk: Contamination via an unusually famous, SEC-documented public incident: Knight Capital's 2012 $440M loss is one of the most heavily circulated case studies in SRE/incident-response training and discourse, and it is even named in this family's own "whyFair" field. A capable agent may pattern-match "this is the Knight Capital story, so check every server before rolling back" and produce cautious, plausible-sounding per-node language without ever performing genuine per-replica reachable-code diagnosis grounded in the specific fictional deployment state it is given. A verifier that can be satisfied by generic caution or by refusing/slow-walking broad remediation across the board -- without verifying the agent correctly distinguished safe from unsafe replicas via the actual reused-identifier/dormant-code mechanism -- would not discriminate the target capability, and is the most likely single point of invalidity; it is also a plausible ground for rejection in official review once the trope is recognized as on-the-nose.
reconciled.semanticOverlapGroup: deployment-rollback-remediation-trap cluster: overlaps in surface theme (rollback-under-uncertainty in deployment/incident-response) with the already-built deployment-rollback-recompute (uncertain-external-effects/duplicate-side-effects, idempotent-recompute mechanism) and deployment-model-alias-rollout-drift (rollout/rollback drift, 20 measured axes), and directly competes for the still-open "deployment-rollback-partial-effects" candidate slot already tracked in this project's own family ledger (confirmed present in data/phase-15-reader-packets.json, data/phase-16-reader-packets.json, and data/phase-novelty-baseline-2026-09.json) -- this is a verified, not speculative, overlap. Its specific mechanism (dormant/deprecated code reactivated by a reused flag or identifier) is mechanistically closer to hidden-environment-dependency + stale-state than to the uncertain-external-effects/duplicate-side-effects pairing used by the already-built rollback families, which is the main source of any genuine novelty here.

family.name: Nominally-Successful Batch Hides Partial Failure
family.definition: Agent submits a multi-resource clinical batch bundle where the outer HTTP response is 200 OK regardless of individual entry outcomes; correct completion requires parsing per-entry status to detect and report which records actually landed.
family.taskShape: Agent submits a batch of related resources, some entries engineered to fail server-side while the batch returns 200; agent must accurately report which resources committed and correctly retry only the failed subset.
family.professionalDomain: healthcare interoperability / clinical data exchange engineering
family.authorityBoundary: Batch requests carry no all-or-nothing guarantee; the agent's authority to declare the workflow done is bounded by per-entry status, not the top-level code.
family.subjectInaccessibleWitness: Whether any entry persisted is not knowable from the outer response; it is only visible in the nested response Bundle.
family.naturalScenarioDimensions: number/type of resources; which subset is engineered to fail and why; transaction vs batch semantics; required follow-up action.
family.whyAgentMayFail: A 200 OK strongly implies success; the spec's batch-semantics carve-out is easy to overlook, so agents checking only the top-level status mis-report partial success as full success.
family.whyFair: This is documented, standard-conformant FHIR behavior, not an undisclosed trick.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage.rationale: Reconciled by evidence weight, not averaging. Normalizing units first: A reported 70 on an implicit 0-100 scale (range 55-85); B reported 0.5 on a 0-1 scale (range 0.4-0.6) = 50 on the same scale. That is a 20-point gap, over the 15-point mandatory-justification threshold. A's estimate is anchored to a real, project-internal measurement -- Phase 14 recorded 8/8 clean solves on the two causally-closest analog families in this portfolio (trading-reconciliation-recompute on uncertain-external-effects; deployment-rollback-recompute on duplicate-side-effects), confirmed in reports/PHASE-14-OPERATOR-EFFECTS.md and reports/hardness-operator-ledger.md -- which is stronger evidence than B's generic appeal to FHIR-corpus memorization. B's one substantive point A does not address -- the task also requires correctly scoping retry to only the failed subset without duplicating side effects, not merely detecting partial failure -- is a real compounding-correctness bar. But Phase 14's analog families already required a comparable detect-then-correctly-act step (recompute / rollback) and still solved 8/8 clean, which undercuts how far that bar should pull the number down. Net: weighted toward A, nudged down for B's compounding-bar point, with a widened range reflecting the genuine conflict between the two evidence bases.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.evidenceUsed: Phase 14 raw agent cells and preregistration (reports/PHASE-14-OPERATOR-EFFECTS.md); null-effect rows for committed-idempotency-authority and recompute-activation-concentration operators (reports/hardness-operator-ledger.md); both scorers' own convergent low subjectInaccessibleAuthority rating (4/10).
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.strongestReasonWrong: If FHIR's fullUrl-vs-positional entry correlation makes selective, non-duplicating retry genuinely harder than the recompute/rollback follow-up Phase 14 tested, the true ordinary-package clean-pass rate could sit meaningfully below 0.62, closer to B's 0.40-0.50 band.

probabilityFullRecipe.rationale: A dropped 70->45 (25pt) and B dropped 50->30 (20pt after normalization) applying a generic 'hardening reduces clean-pass' heuristic -- yet each one's own strongestReasonWrong flags that Phase 14 measured a NULL EFFECT from this project's standard hardening bundle on the two closest analog families (still 8/8 clean after hardening). Neither scorer actually incorporated that self-identified counter-evidence into their point estimate; both discounted anyway. Correcting for that shared blind spot pulls the reconciled full-recipe estimate much closer to the reconciled ordinary-package estimate (0.62) than either scorer's own number, while still crediting some real uplift from B's concretely-proposed, not-yet-tested distractors (fullUrl-vs-positional correlation ambiguity, retriable-vs-permanent failure-reason confusion, mixed batch/transaction-mode bundles), which fall outside what Phase 14 actually exercised and so aren't covered by its null-effect finding. This is a genuine reasoned departure from both inputs, not a midpoint average of 37.5.
probabilityFullRecipe.evidenceUsed: Same Phase 14 null-effect evidence, read here as a correction to both scorers' hardening-discount heuristic rather than as an added caution.
probabilityFullRecipe.strongestReasonWrong: If B's proposed distractors are exactly the kind of surface variation Phase 14's concentrated-activation operator already implicitly covers, the null-effect result transfers directly and the true full-recipe number could sit much lower, near B's 0.30, or track the ordinary-package number almost exactly -- i.e. hardening may add close to zero discriminating power on this axis no matter how it's dressed.

reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
Two deltas required explicit reconciliation rather than averaging.

(1) MANDATORY -- probabilityOrdinaryPackage: the raw inputs (A=70, B=0.5) look close in digits but are on different scales -- A used an implicit 0-100 convention (its own range 55-85 confirms this), B used a 0-1 fraction (range 0.4-0.6). Normalized to the same scale, A=70 vs B=50 is a 20-point gap, over the 15-point threshold. Root cause of the *substantive* disagreement (not just the units bug): A weights a real project-internal measurement (Phase 14: 8/8 clean solves on the two causally-closest analog families, trading-reconciliation-recompute and deployment-rollback-recompute, verified in reports/PHASE-14-OPERATOR-EFFECTS.md and reports/hardness-operator-ledger.md) more heavily than B's generic FHIR-training-corpus argument. B's one point A misses -- selective, non-duplicating retry is a real compounding-correctness bar beyond mere detection -- is legitimate but is undercut by the fact that Phase 14's analogs already had a comparable detect+correctly-act requirement and still hit 8/8. Reconciled at 0.62 (leaning toward A's better-evidenced number, nudged down for B's valid but only partially-supported point), not the arithmetic mean.

(2) probabilityFullRecipe: A's 45 vs B's 30 (normalized) is a 15-point gap -- exactly at, not over, the mandatory threshold, but flagged anyway because it shares the same root cause as (1). Both scorers apply a generic "hardening lowers pass rate" discount from their own ordinary-package number, and both scorers' own strongestReasonWrong fields point out that this contradicts the same Phase 14 null-effect finding they cited for question (1) -- the standard hardening bundle produced zero effect (still 8/8 clean) on the closest analogs. Neither actually corrected their point estimate for their own cited counter-evidence. The reconciled value (0.50) corrects that shared blind spot by pulling the full-recipe estimate much closer to the reconciled ordinary-package estimate than either scorer proposed, while still allowing modest uplift for B's concretely novel (untested-by-Phase-14) distractor ideas.

(3) opportunityScoreTotal (61 vs 68, delta=7) is under the 10-point mandatory threshold, but component decomposition surfaced a real inconsistency worth correcting rather than passing through: Scorer B rated latentDiagnosisReasoningBurden at the maximum, 10/10, and naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace at 9/10, while B's own principalValidityRisk (shared verbatim in spirit with A's) argues the central trap is a single synchronous parse away, not genuine multi-hop diagnosis -- a near-maximum reasoning-burden score directly contradicts that stated risk. Both scorers independently converged on a low subjectInaccessibleAuthority (4/10) and low implementationTrialTractability (4/10), which is internally consistent with a *modest*, not maximal, reasoning-burden score. Reconciled scoreBreakdown pulls latentDiagnosisReasoningBurden to 7 and naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace to 7 (A's more internally-consistent values), keeps noveltyPortfolioContribution at A's lower 2 (both scorers flag heavy semantic overlap with two already-shipped, already-null-effect analog families in this portfolio -- the "don't optimize for a flattering result" instruction argues for taking the more skeptical of two converging low-novelty scores, not splitting the difference upward), and takes B's slightly higher authoritativeProvenance (7, since FHIR batch-vs-transaction semantics are normative spec text, a genuinely authoritative source, not just one incident writeup). Net effect: reconciled opportunityScoreTotal=60, essentially A's number, because the correction targets exactly the components where B's narrative and B's own scores were in tension with each other.

(4) officialReviewProbability (A=0.4, B=0.5, delta=0.1, under threshold) reconciled to 0.4, the more cautious figure, consistent with the overall skepticism justified above: heavy semantic overlap with an already-measured, already-null-effect family cluster plus a weak subject-inaccessible-witness claim are real headwinds to a review panel's enthusiasm. tenDistinctTaskProbability (0.75/0.75) needed no reconciliation. firstPackageBuildHours (30 vs 16) and marginalBuildHours (8 vs 4) were not covered by the mandatory-delta rule but are reconciled to 24 and 6 respectively, leaning toward A's higher estimate since the verified need for idempotent, selectively-scoped retry (B's own point) adds real verifier and harness complexity beyond a bare detection check.

Overall: this reconciliation is not a flattering result for the family -- it holds opportunityScoreTotal near the lower of the two inputs, keeps the probability-of-clean-pass estimates closer to the higher (more concerning, less-discriminating) end, and takes the more skeptical value wherever the two scorers converged on a low score or where one scorer's narrative contradicted its own numeric rating.

family.name: Silent Scope Narrowing on Token Refresh
family.definition: Agent refreshes an OAuth2 credential mid-task expecting unchanged authority, but the authorization server silently returns a narrower scope per RFC 6749; correct behavior requires parsing the refresh response's scope field and adjusting subsequent calls rather than assuming prior permissions still hold.
family.taskShape: Agent performs an authorized action, its token is refreshed mid-trajectory with a silently narrowed scope, and a later downstream action depending on the original scope must be detected as now-unauthorized via the response body rather than a late 403.
family.professionalDomain: identity and access management / OAuth2 client integration engineering
family.authorityBoundary: The refreshed token's actual scope is authoritative over the agent's assumed scope; the server may narrow it without prominent warning per spec, so the client must read the response, not assume.
family.subjectInaccessibleWitness: The server-side decision to narrow scope is opaque; only the scope field in the refresh response and eventual call outcomes reveal it.
family.naturalScenarioDimensions: which permission is narrowed; number of downstream calls depending on lost scope; proactive scope-parsing vs discovery-via-failure; single vs chained refreshes.
family.whyAgentMayFail: Agents treat refresh success as full authority restored and skip the optional scope field, executing downstream calls under a false assumption and failing several steps later with a hard-to-diagnose late 403.
family.whyFair: The rule is explicit in RFC 6749 and load-bearing for any refresh implementation; correctly parsing a documented response field is core, non-obscure API-integration competence.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage.rationale: Both scorers land within 10pp of each other (A=45, B=35), under the 15pp mandatory-justification threshold, so this is a reasoned midpoint rather than a forced reconciliation. A's construction-gap argument (leaky starter hint, non-strict downstream mock, verifier checking only final call success) and B's harness-verbosity argument (a well-built tool wrapper surfaces the full refresh JSON verbatim, making narrowed scope visible text rather than a suppressed signal) are both live and point in opposite directions on the same uncertain variable -- how the ordinary package's harness renders the refresh response -- so the reconciled estimate sits at the arithmetic center with a wide band rather than favoring either failure story.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.evidenceUsed: Same qualitative pattern both scorers cite (sibling permission-boundary families in this portfolio have shipped leaking starters or decision-string-only verifiers) plus B's harness-transcript-verbosity consideration; no measured clean-pass-rate data exists yet for this exact family.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.strongestReasonWrong: If this portfolio's actual harness convention (as built for the three sibling scope-narrowing families) is to hand the subject the full raw API response object rather than a summarized token, the true rate could sit above 60% purely as a read-comprehension check, which neither scorer's point estimate captures well.

probabilityFullRecipe.rationale: A=20 and B=15 differ by only 5pp, well under the 15pp threshold, so this is a straightforward reasoned midpoint. Both scorers agree a fully hardened package (buried scope field, rarely-invoked downstream dependency, chained refreshes) should suppress clean-pass rate well below the ordinary-package estimate, and both independently flag that a single-hop, non-obscure spec check leaves headroom for a well-primed frontier agent to comply reliably even under hardening -- pulling the estimate up from a naive 'hardened-so-near-zero' assumption.
probabilityFullRecipe.evidenceUsed: Judgment prior only, as both scorers state; no mutant-fatality, reward-zero, or trial data exists for this specific family. Comparable built sibling families (access-token-scope-expansion, delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation) have real trial ledgers in this repo (data/phase-16-source-ledger.json) but their measured rates were not supplied to either scorer and are not substituted here.
probabilityFullRecipe.strongestReasonWrong: OAuth refresh-response handling is common in coding/agent training corpora; if the specific 'scope may narrow silently, always re-check the field' pattern is well-represented there, a maximally hardened package could still see clean rates well above 28% because the trick is memorized rather than reasoned through, exactly as B's own strongestReasonWrong argues.

reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
Trigger: opportunityScoreTotal differs by 17 points (59 vs 76), exceeding the 10-point threshold, so this requires explicit justification rather than averaging to ~67.5. Both probability deltas (10pp and 5pp) are under the 15pp threshold and were reconciled by ordinary reasoned midpoint above.

Decomposing the 17-point gap dimension-by-dimension (B minus A): authoritativeProvenance +1, economicValue +1, latentDiagnosisReasoningBurden +2, naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace +6, subjectInaccessibleAuthority 0, verifierAntiCheatFeasibility +2, constructionOperatorCompatibility +1, materiallyDistinctInstanceCapacity +2, implementationTrialTractability +1, noveltyPortfolioContribution +1. Nine of ten dimensions show a small, consistent +0-to-+2 lean by Scorer B -- a mild, unremarkable calibration difference, resolved below by taking values close to the midpoint or slightly toward whichever scorer's own reasoning was better supported per dimension. The tenth, naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace (6 vs 12), single-handedly accounts for 6 of the 17 total points (over one-third of the gap) and is the actual reason this family cleared the 10-point threshold at all.

I discount Scorer B's 12 on naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace rather than averaging it, for three concrete reasons: (1) it is a statistical outlier against both scorers' own behavior -- across all 20 sub-scores in this pair, every other value both raters ever assigned falls in 1-9, so 12 sits ~33% above the ceiling either rater used anywhere else, with no accompanying rationale text that explains why this one dimension should break that pattern; (2) it is internally inconsistent with Scorer B's own semanticOverlapGroup writeup, which states this family has "near-total" overlap with access-token-scope-expansion on the exact permission-boundary/scope-narrowing axis -- a family whose adversarial-scenario space is largely already claimed by an existing family cannot simultaneously score exceptionally high on *adding* natural adversarial scenario space to the portfolio; (3) I verified this overlap directly against the repository rather than taking either scorer's word for it: data/phase-novelty-baseline-2026-09.json (the frozen built-family list used for blind novelty review) lists access-token-scope-expansion, delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation, and prompt-injection-approval-scope-drift as already-built portfolio families sharing the exact permission-boundary + stale-state mechanism pair this candidate proposes, and data/phase-16-source-ledger.json shows real, dated trial runs (2026-08) for two of the three. This is not a hypothetical or idea-stage sibling set -- it is concretely built and trialed, which sharply caps how much genuinely new adversarial scenario space this family can add. I set the reconciled value at 7: above A's 6 (the family's 4 explicit knobs -- which permission, call count, proactive-vs-reactive, chained-vs-single -- do add some real combinatorial texture A's rationale undersells) but far below B's 12.

Other dimension resolutions: latentDiagnosisReasoningBurden (7->8, favoring B) because the whyAgentMayFail text explicitly describes a multi-step-removed, hard-to-diagnose late-403 failure, which both scorers' own prose supports at the higher end. verifierAntiCheatFeasibility (6->6, favoring A) because both scorers' principalValidityRisk sections independently converge on the same live, unresolved anti-cheat gap (blanket-caution or reactive-403-recovery passing as proactive scope detection) -- a risk this explicitly shared and unresolved should not be scored optimistically. materiallyDistinctInstanceCapacity (5/7->6) as a reasoned midpoint given the identical tenDistinctTaskProbability=0.75 both scorers independently produced. noveltyPortfolioContribution held at the floor (1, A's value, not B's 2) given the now-confirmed concrete overlap with built siblings sharing identical mechanism tags.

Net effect: reconciled opportunityScoreTotal = 62, closer to Scorer A's 59 than to Scorer B's 76 and below the naive blind average of 67.5 -- a deliberately unflattering correction, made because the dominant contributor to B's higher total (naturalAdversarialScenarioSpace) fails on internal consistency and is directly contradicted by verifiable in-repo evidence of heavy, already-realized portfolio overlap, not because B's overall optimism was baseless on the other nine dimensions.
reconciled.cheapestFalsifyingProbe: Two-stage cheap probe, run before any real infrastructure spend: (1) construct validity check (B's probe) -- stand up the mock refresh endpoint + one downstream resource endpoint with a narrowed scope in the refresh response, and run 3-5 frontier agents zero-shot (no hint, normal verbose tool-response transcript) through one instance each; if most already notice and adapt to the narrowing, the family's core 'natural silent-failure trap' premise is falsified cheaply. (2) verifier validity check (A's probe) -- separately run a scripted known-bad 'refresh-then-blindly-proceed' subject against the same mock + verifier; if it still passes because the downstream mock doesn't strictly gate on scope or the verifier checks only final success/absence-of-raw-403 rather than call ordering, the mechanism is unverifiable regardless of how agents behave. Both checks are single-instance, pre-mutant-infrastructure, and target the two independent ways this family's premise could fail (too easy for good agents, or too gameable for bad ones).
reconciled.principalValidityRisk: Two compounding, independently-raised risks, neither resolved by construction alone: (1) Verifier/anti-cheat gap (both scorers, and explicitly the same gap this portfolio's closest built sibling already shipped with): a subject can pass via blanket caution (re-confirm or abstain after every refresh) or reactive 403-recovery without ever parsing or reasoning about the scope field, functionally indistinguishable from genuine proactive detection unless the harness instruments call order and field access directly. (2) Construct-validity is harness-contingent (Scorer B): whether the tool wrapper surfaces the full refresh JSON body verbatim (trivial read-comprehension) or abstracts it to a bare token string (genuinely silent narrowing) flips this family from 'hard natural trap' to 'trivial check' independent of any agent's actual capability. Confirmed via direct repo inspection (data/phase-novelty-baseline-2026-09.json, data/phase-16-source-ledger.json): this also substantially overlaps two already-built, already-trialed portfolio families (access-token-scope-expansion, delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation) sharing the identical permission-boundary + stale-state mechanism pair, so even a well-constructed package risks adding a redundant signal rather than a materially new one.
reconciled.semanticOverlapGroup: authority-boundary-scope-narrowing / stale-assumed-authority-vs-current-grant cluster -- confirmed (not merely asserted by the scorers) near-total mechanism overlap with access-token-scope-expansion and delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation, both listed as already-built, already-trialed portfolio families in data/phase-novelty-baseline-2026-09.json sharing this family's exact permission-boundary + stale-state mechanism tags, plus prompt-injection-approval-scope-drift (permission-boundary + stale-state + context-contamination). All four test the same underlying shape -- agent trusts a cached/assumed authority instead of reconciling against the current authoritative grant -- varied only by domain (OAuth refresh vs wallet delegation vs prompt-injection-driven approval drift vs this candidate's refresh-response scope field).

family.name: SQL/Query Identifier Injection Scope Expansion
family.definition: User- or upstream-tool-controlled identifiers (database/schema/table names, search query strings) are interpolated unsanitized into an executed data-tool call, letting a crafted or unusual identifier value cause the tool to read/touch objects far outside its nominally narrow, declared scope.
family.taskShape: Agent is asked to perform a narrowly-scoped lookup (inspect a named schema/table, search a named spreadsheet) where the identifier may originate from an earlier, less-trusted step; agent must validate/parameterize the identifier rather than trust direct string interpolation, and a verifier checks whether the resulting action stayed within the intended object scope.
family.professionalDomain: data warehousing / spreadsheet API integration security engineering
family.authorityBoundary: The credential/session's nominal authority is scoped to the specific object named in the request; unsanitized interpolation lets a crafted identifier value silently expand that authority to arbitrary objects the underlying credential can reach.
family.subjectInaccessibleWitness: The agent (or its verifier) cannot tell from the tool's successful response alone whether the query executed against the intended object or a different one reached via injection -- only an independent diff of actual queried objects reveals scope expansion.
family.naturalScenarioDimensions: identifier source (user-typed vs chained from a prior tool's output); injection surface (SQL f-string vs Drive query string); presence/absence of an allow-list; error-vs-silent-success on malformed identifiers.
family.whyAgentMayFail: An agent implementing or using such a tool with a plausible-looking, narrow-sounding request will not notice that a crafted schema name or quote character breaks out of the intended query scope, because the call still returns a well-formed, plausible-looking result.
family.whyFair: Unsanitized identifier interpolation causing injection is a textbook, well-documented software security defect (CWE-class), independently confirmed via a filed and reviewed PR -- not obscure or proprietary.

probabilityOrdinaryPackage.rationale: Both scorers independently describe the same bimodal structure (agent never notices the trust boundary at all -> low measured pass rate ~15-20%, vs. agent applies partial/generic validation that clears a not-fully-comprehensive ordinary verifier -> high measured pass rate ~70-80%) but land on different central tendencies (A=50%, B's stated 0.3 corresponds, once its own framing is taken at face value, to a lower-pass-rate lean). I verified a concrete, on-axis precedent in this repository rather than trusting either scorer's abstract appeal to 'project history': campaigns/access-token-scope-expansion-2026-08.json's slot note records that the FIRST build of access-token-scope-expansion (same authority-boundary-scope-violation causal axis) shipped a starter that was already a complete passing solution, whose scope_bound_exactly check never actually inspected the issued grant, producing a false 384/384-clean pass that had to be discarded and rebuilt under a new challenge hash. That is exactly the 'ordinary package construction accidentally trivializes itself' failure mode both scorers hypothesize, now confirmed to have actually happened once already on this exact causal axis in this project. That tips the central estimate toward the higher-pass-rate mode.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.evidenceUsed: Klavis PR defect confirmation (both scorers); campaigns/access-token-scope-expansion-2026-08.json verified in-repo (this reconciliation) showing a real prior instance of an ordinary-quality build on the same causal axis producing a trivially-passing artifact due to an incomplete verifier check.
probabilityOrdinaryPackage.strongestReasonWrong: If the package author is explicitly warned off the access-token precedent and builds a comprehensive per-site check from the start, realized pass rate could fall back toward the 'agent never validates at all' low mode (~20-30%), well below this estimate -- the access-token precedent is suggestive, not dispositive, since it was a distinct implementation with its own specific verifier bug.

probabilityFullRecipe.rationale: Raw values (A: 20% pass rate; B: 0.55) look 35 points apart, but they are not measuring the same construct. A directly states a per-trial agent-pass probability throughout ('true pass rate... 15-20%... 75%+'). B's own evidenceUsed field frames its number in terms of 'a clean 5/6-6/6 outcome requires roughly 80-90% per-trial failure rates' -- i.e. B is estimating the probability of clearing this project's multi-trial success bar, not the per-trial pass probability itself. I checked this against docs/INHERITED-EVIDENCE.md section 1's own documented binomial model (P(>=5 of 6 fail) as a function of per-trial p): inverting B's stated 0.55 through that table implies a per-trial p of roughly 0.20-0.25 -- which nearly coincides with A's directly-stated 0.20. So the two estimates are far more consistent than their headline numbers suggest once put on a common basis. I set the reconciled per-trial-p estimate slightly above A's point value because docs/INHERITED-EVIDENCE.md's calibration table records 0.35-0.55 as the best FLOOR previously achieved (not a ceiling) for the only two discovery shapes 'worth building on' ('confirmed green measurement' / 'abstraction the model must justify but cannot'), and this family has not yet demonstrated it can beat that floor the way the source project's one genuine 6/6 mechanism did (which required a model-specific systematic blind spot, not a generic textbook CWE pattern).
probabilityFullRecipe.evidenceUsed: docs/INHERITED-EVIDENCE.md sections 1-2 (binomial model and calibration table, verified in-repo); A's per-site-enumerable construction argument (21 known call sites); B's explicit 80-90%-per-trial-failure framing.
probabilityFullRecipe.strongestReasonWrong: If the identifier-vs-value distinction is genuinely rarely internalized even by security-tuned agents (B's own strongestReasonWrong), true p could sit well under 0.15 and reliable 6/6 becomes achievable; conversely, A's own cheapestFalsifyingProbe explicitly predicts a security-framed ask could one-shot a full pass via memorized CWE-89 recall, which would push true p toward the same 0.5+ zone as the ordinary-package case regardless of construction effort.

reconciled.reconciliationNotes:
Two things needed resolving before any comparison was meaningful, and averaging the raw numbers would have been wrong on both counts.

(1) Units mismatch, mechanical: Scorer A expressed probabilityOrdinaryPackage/probabilityFullRecipe on a 0-100 scale (50, 20; ranges 30-65, 10-35). Scorer B expressed the same fields on a 0-1 scale (0.3, 0.55; ranges 0.2-0.45, 0.4-0.7). Naive numeric comparison of "50 vs 0.3" or "20 vs 0.55" is meaningless; normalized to a common percentage basis the gaps are 20pp (ordinary) and 35pp (full recipe) -- both exceed the 15pp reconciliation trigger.

(2) Construct mismatch, substantive and more important: even normalized, A and B are not estimating the same quantity for probabilityFullRecipe. A states throughout that its number is a per-trial agent-pass probability. B's own evidenceUsed cites this project's documented need for "roughly 80-90% per-trial failure rates" to clear a 5/6-6/6 bar -- i.e. B's 0.55 is closer to "probability the recipe clears the multi-trial bar" than to per-trial p. I cross-checked this using docs/INHERITED-EVIDENCE.md's own binomial table (verified in-repo, not assumed): inverting B's 0.55 through P(>=5 of 6 fail) implies a per-trial p of ~0.20-0.25, which nearly coincides with A's directly-stated 0.20. So most of the apparent 35-point full-recipe gap is a units/definitional artifact, not a real disagreement about difficulty -- I resolved it by converging on a per-trial-p convention (0.28, informed slightly upward by the calibration table's documented 0.35-0.55 floor for this discovery shape) rather than splitting the raw 20/55 difference.

For probabilityOrdinaryPackage the same translation narrows but does not close the gap (A's 50% implies a very low ~11% bar-clearing probability via that table; B's stated 30% implies a per-trial p of ~35%, versus A's direct 50% -- a residual ~15pp gap in implied p). I did not average this away. Instead I checked this project's own history directly rather than trusting either scorer's abstract citation of it: campaigns/access-token-scope-expansion-2026-08.json (verified in-repo) shows that the first build of access-token-scope-expansion -- the most directly comparable already-built family on the same authority-boundary-scope-violation causal axis -- shipped a starter that was already a complete passing solution, with a verifier check that never actually inspected the issued grant, producing a false 384/384 clean pass that had to be discarded and rebuilt under a new hash. That is a concrete, confirmed instance of exactly the "ordinary package turns out easier than intended" failure mode both scorers only argued for hypothetically. This tips my final ordinary-package estimate toward the higher end of the two scorers' central tendencies (0.55) rather than toward the midpoint or toward B's more conservative reading -- this is evidence-driven, not a flattering-result push (a higher probabilityOrdinaryPackage here signals a *weaker* opportunity: less true difficulty, more risk the family measures verifier laxity rather than agent capability).

On scoreBreakdown (delta 65 vs 67, within the 10-point tolerance, no mandatory justification required but reconciled anyway): eight of ten sub-scores were within 1 point and simply averaged with conservative (round-down) tie-breaking. subjectInaccessibleAuthority was raised from A's 6 toward B's 8 (settled at 7) because the family definition's own subjectInaccessibleWitness field explicitly states the agent/verifier cannot tell success from silent scope-expansion without an independent object-touched diff -- that text substantiates B's higher rating better than A's. noveltyPortfolioContribution (2/2, both agree) and implementationTrialTractability (4/4, both agree) were left untouched -- both scorers converge that this family is a weak-novelty, awkward-to-build addition, and I am preserving that unflattering convergence rather than smoothing it over.

Both scorers' principalValidityRisk sections are correct and complementary, not competing: A's correction that the "independently confirmed via a filed and reviewed PR" provenance claim overstates the evidence (both cited Klavis PRs were never reviewed and auto-closed after 21 days, though the defect is genuinely live) should stand as written. B's requirement that scope-violation ground truth come from an audit channel the subject cannot reach or shape is the more concrete anti-cheat risk and is independently grounded in this repo's own grader-privilege-boundary mechanism (data/mechanisms.json, docs/families/permission-boundary-tools.md, verified in-repo) -- both should be carried forward together. Net assessment: this is a moderate, not flattering, opportunity -- real and independently-verified defect, but heavily overlapping the portfolio's existing authority-boundary-scope-violation axis (access-token-scope-expansion, delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation, killed route-scope-expansion-probe), low novelty contribution, and now-confirmed (not just theoretical) risk that an ordinary-quality build on this axis previously produced a trivially-passing artifact in this very project.
reconciled.cheapestFalsifyingProbe: Run B's zero-cost check first: against the mock backend alone, feed a known-good reference (proper allow-listing) and a known-bad stub (naive interpolation) the identical crafted identifier, and confirm the independent object-touched diff (not the subject's own tool response) discriminates bad from good and rejects malformed identifiers -- this falsifies a verifier that can't discriminate genuine scope violation before any paid trial runs. If that passes, proceed to A's single ungated frontier-agent smoke trial with the bare, non-security-framed task; a one-shot full pass under the real per-site verifier exposes the family as known-pattern recall rather than a genuine discriminator.
reconciled.principalValidityRisk: Two compounding risks, both verified rather than assumed. (1) Ceiling-effect/pattern-memorization: allow-listing identifiers before interpolation is textbook, heavily-trained CWE-89 remediation, and the family duplicates the causal axis (authority-boundary-scope-violation / missing-validation-widens-declared-scope) already occupied by access-token-scope-expansion, delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation, and the killed route-scope-expansion-probe candidate -- confirmed by both scorers and consistent with this repo's own family-diversity.md listing. (2) Verifier ground truth must come from an audit path the subject cannot reach or shape (an independent query/access log), never from parsing the subject's own SQL/query string or trusting its tool response -- this is the same shared-authority hole this project's own grader-privilege-boundary mechanism catalogues (verified present in data/mechanisms.json and docs/families/permission-boundary-tools.md), and campaigns/access-token-scope-expansion-2026-08.json shows a concrete prior instance, on this same causal axis, of a verifier check that didn't actually inspect the thing it claimed to grade.
