- verifier-process-and-ledger-isolation -> the system-of-record store is a separate process/service the agent's submitted artifacts have no write access to except through audited tool calls; [HARDENED] this claim now ships with a negative control (narrowDevMutants #8): a deliberately-writable canary build the same boundary must be shown to catch, not merely asserted to hold.
- a2-explicit-terminal-state-repair -> the visible spec explicitly states which submitted artifacts are final-of-record per stage, without naming any historical anti-pattern.
- narrow-mutant-isolation -> each dev mutant drops or corrupts exactly one carried-forward fact category (or, for #7, one write-path integrity property), holding the rest of the environment fixed, so a failure attributes to one mechanism.
- b6-rig-integrity-controls -> every scenario rig must show reference passes clean, each targeted mutant fails only its own checks, and malformed/absent submissions are refused; [HARDENED] extended with a store-forgery/tool-bypass mutant (narrowDevMutants #7) so the WRITE boundary, not only the READ (day-gating) boundary, is exercised.
- committed-idempotency-authority -> native analog "persisted-record-over-recompute": the correct approach commits each day's authoritative fact into the agent's own running state when learned and reads that persisted record later. [HARDENED] At least two graded facts per instance must additionally be DERIVED values requiring synthesis across multiple independently-arriving upstream facts under an explicit domain reconciliation policy (proration, netting, or compound multi-field consistency for an overlap entity) -- a single field substituted for another is insufficient by construction, closing the "repeated simple substitution" gap two skeptics identified.
- narrow-recompute-starter -> if any starter scaffold is provided, it may show the tempting "always look up the current value" pattern on one non-graded example category only, never on the graded one.
- fuzz-controlling-parameter -> fuzz (stage count, event placement, fan-out, richness, time budget, synthesis-density, overlap-count) to locate the activation region.
- recompute-activation-concentration -> [HARDENED] concretely floored at >=4 independently-verifiable graded facts per instance, >=2 requiring synthesis, and >=1 entity touched by 2+ overlapping drift categories, enforced as killConditions #7 (previously an implicit/aspirational goal with no numeric floor).
recipeCards.nonApplicableOperators:
- Recipe point 3 as literally stated (a defect embedded in existing code that the agent must locate and repair) does not apply: there is no codebase with a bug to find. It is reframed instead as a naturally superseding fact (see outboxOperatorMapping #3).
- Crash-injection, lease/epoch fencing tokens, and duplicate-side-effect/exactly-once tool-retry semantics do not apply verbatim: there is no single external side-effecting call with an ambiguous UNKNOWN completion status, and no natural process-crash surface. Random crashes or lease revocations would be unnatural here and are explicitly excluded.
- A literal append-only "outbox" ledger structure is not the family's natural witness; the natural external authority is a system-of-record store fed by day-gated events -- functionally analogous (subject-inaccessible, tool-mediated, verifier-read) but not an outbox.
- "duplicate-side-effects" style dedup concerns are not central: this family is about information fidelity across simulated time, not avoiding a repeated external effect under retry.
- Idempotency-key recovery across "lease epochs" specifically does not transfer; the native analog kept is only the shape "persist now, do not recompute later," not the mechanics of keys, leases, or epochs.
- [HARDENED, clarifying] The newly-added store-forgery dev mutant (narrowDevMutants #7) and leaky-variant canary (#8) test only whether the tool-mediated WRITE boundary is a hard sandbox boundary; they are not a reintroduction of crash/lease/exactly-once semantics, which remain excluded for the reasons above. They exist because two skeptics correctly noted that no mutant previously tested writing/forging the record directly (only reading ahead was tested), not because the outbox's retry mechanics have become relevant.
recipeCards.familyNativeDifficultyOperators:
- persisted-record-over-recompute (difficulty): correct execution requires committing each day's authoritative fact into a running state artifact when learned, then reading that persisted record downstream; an agent that instead recomputes from final-day evidence gets it wrong because final-day evidence is deliberately insufficient.
- multi-fact synthesis over field substitution (difficulty, construction requirement) [HARDENED, new]: at least two graded facts per instance must be DERIVED values combining two or more independently-arriving upstream facts under an explicit domain reconciliation policy (proration, netting, or compound multi-field consistency for an entity touched by overlapping events). A plain "copy the latest value into the field" substitution is insufficient by construction and is the excluded thin-reference shape (killConditions #7) that review identified as structurally identical to CAA's "one rule applied repeatedly."
- tamper-resistant write boundary (validity-control, family-native) [HARDENED, new]: the tool-mediated write path into the system-of-record must be a hard sandbox boundary, proven with a store-forgery mutant and a deliberately-leaky canary variant (narrowDevMutants #7-8), not merely asserted -- an unproven write-boundary claim is the same unfalsifiable-isolation pattern this repo's Phase 16 CAA controls already exhibited once.
- simulated-time information gating / non-re-derivability (validity-control, family-native): at least one graded fact must be genuinely unrecoverable from what remains accessible at the end of the horizon, tested by the last-day-cram mutant.
- silent narrow propagation (the causal claim itself): a single dropped or drifted upstream fact must propagate to exactly the final deliverables that legitimately depend on it and no others.
- time-budget sensitivity (scenario-selection): time budget must be a first-class fuzzed dimension, not held constant by accident.
recipeCards.multiFileCodebaseSketch:
A single environment root per scenario instance, e.g.:

- inbox/day1/ ... inbox/dayN/ -- memos, emails, corrected data files, and policy updates; each day's directory is unreadable (or absent) until the agent advances the simulated clock past that day. Frozen and hashed at authoring time.
- state/ -- the agent's own running record, its authoritative memory of what it has learned and decided; this is where "persisted-record-over-recompute" either happens or doesn't. [HARDENED] No annotation convention is mandated or expected here anymore -- the earlier draft's "provenance annotation" idea is removed; whatever the agent writes here is never read by the verifier or by any coverage predictor.
- tools/ -- CLI wrappers standing in for real professional systems. [HARDENED] Mounted read-only to the agent (or run as a separate process the agent has no filesystem access to); calling a tool is the only way to write to the external system-of-record, and each successful call produces a hashed receipt logged append-only outside the agent's writable sandbox.
- self-check/day-end-checklist -- validates per-day submission completeness and schema shape only; exposes no other signal.
- outbound/ -- the agent's final deliverables, also read by the private verifier alongside the system-of-record.
- (private, not in the agent's tree) system-of-record/ -- the authoritative external store, populated independently by the harness, mutated only through tools/ calls with a matching receipt, read only by the isolated post-hoc verifier.
- (construction-time only, never shipped to the agent or the runtime verifier) dev/self-check-archetypes/ -- the fixed library of generic, domain-agnostic archetype scripts (completeness-only, same-day-only, final-day full-recency, changed-since-last-touch) used once, at authoring time, to compute the self-check-coverage predictor against the frozen reference and dev mutants. [HARDENED, new]
- (construction-time only) a leaky-variant canary build -- the same instance with tools/ made agent-writable or the store directly mounted read-write, used once to prove the isolation/tamper detector catches a real leak, then discarded. [HARDENED, new]

Enough real subsystems that no single file or command holds the whole task.
recipeCards.publicOutcomeRequirements: [HARDENED] Stated only as ordinary professional accuracy/currency expectations, in the same words a real assignment brief would use -- never as a description of the test mechanism, never naming "drift," "carryforward," "supersession," or the fact that intermediate days carry no feedback. General template: "By the end of day N, every deliverable in outbound/ must be submitted through the provided tools, schema-valid, and accurate as of the moment you submit it, for each item you are responsible for." Each instance then states its own ordinary domain-accuracy clause in place of a meta rule, e.g. (procurement): "A submitted PO reconciliation must reflect the vendor's current price, the PO's current cost-center allocation, and the quantity actually received." This is table-stakes professional language -- accuracy and currency are assumed of any real submission -- not a hint about what is checked, how many facts are checked, or which day is load-bearing. The previous draft's explicit sentence ("information you receive on a given day supersedes anything you were told earlier... you will not receive feedback on intermediate days; only the end state is evaluated") is removed from public text: two independent skeptics flagged it as functionally equivalent to CAA1 stating its own tested mechanism outright. That content still describes a true property of the harness, but it is now discovered operationally (through day-gating and the absence of any response to submissions) rather than announced -- see infoIntentionallyAbsent.
recipeCards.infoIntentionallyAbsent:
- Which specific fact(s) are actually checked at the end (the graded subset is a proper subset of everything touched).
- Which day's event is "load-bearing" for which deliverable (the fan-out structure).
- That a private system-of-record exists, its schema, or that it is the source of truth read by the verifier.
- That the day-end checklist has a known coverage gap, or what that gap is.
- The narrow-mutant taxonomy or the existence of held-out validation scenarios.
- Per-fact scoring weights or partial-credit rules (there are none).
- That recomputing everything from final-day evidence alone is insufficient by design.
- [HARDENED, new] That intermediate days carry no feedback signal and only final state is evaluated -- a property of the harness the agent may infer from the absence of any response to its actions, never stated in the brief.
- [HARDENED, new] That the recency/supersession logic is "the rule being tested" -- the brief states only ordinary domain accuracy/currency expectations in the same words a real assignment would use, never a labeled meta-rule.
- [HARDENED, new] That a construction-time self-check-coverage predictor, an isolation canary, or a store-forgery mutant were used to build or validate this instance.
- [HARDENED, new] Which graded facts require synthesis versus substitution, or that any distinction between the two exists.
recipeCards.visibleTestStrategy: A day-end self-check tool the agent may run any number of times: it validates that each day's required submissions exist, are well-formed, and were made through the correct tool. It deliberately does not check cross-day numerical or logical consistency against superseded values. [HARDENED] It exposes no other diagnostic signal -- no annotation count, no coverage score, nothing beyond bare completeness/schema pass-fail. The prior draft's "provenance annotation count, surfaced as a self-check-coverage predictor" is removed entirely: it was computed from the agent's own writable state fields, required an unmandated annotation convention a fully-correct agent might never use, and was consulted by the private verifier for diagnostics -- three independent skeptics identified this as the same self-declared, gameable evidence the verifier architecture claims never to trust. This narrow scope mirrors a realistic professional day-end checklist (did you file it) rather than a full audit; the gap is source-supported by the family's own claim that no intermediate checkpoint signal exists for carryforward correctness. A genuine self-check-coverage predictor does exist for this family, but it now lives entirely at construction time, outside the agent's environment and outside the runtime verifier -- see scenarioSelectionStrategy and privateVerifierArchitecture.
recipeCards.externalAuthorityOrWitness:
Two paired, subject-inaccessible authorities:
1. The day-gated event feed -- authored and hashed before the run, released only as the agent advances the simulated clock. The agent cannot read ahead or retroactively edit an earlier day.
2. The tool-mediated system-of-record store -- the authoritative record of final state, which the agent can only extend through defined professional tool calls. [HARDENED] This is now an enforced hard sandbox boundary, not an asserted convention: tools/ is mounted read-only to the agent (or run as a separate process it cannot write to), and every successful tool call produces a hashed receipt logged append-only outside the agent's writable sandbox; the private verifier treats any store entry lacking a matching receipt as an automatic fail. This claim ships with two negative controls that did not exist in the prior draft: a store-forgery mutant (narrowDevMutants #7) that attempts to write the store or fabricate a receipt directly, which must be blocked or detected; and a deliberately-leaky canary build (narrowDevMutants #8) that must be caught by the same detector, proving the detector can catch a real leak rather than merely never firing -- the specific repair this repo's own Phase 17 postmortem (recommendation #5) prescribes for exactly the two Phase 16 CAA controls (witnessIsolated, challengeNonleakage) that had no reachable failing branch.
recipeCards.fuzzerDimensions:
- number of dependent stages/simulated days
- number of independent drift-event categories in flight concurrently (fan-out and interleaving)
- which day each event is introduced
- how many downstream deliverables a single event legitimately touches
- environment richness (number of subsystems/files/tools in play)
- execution/time budget
- presence of distractor events that must explicitly NOT be carried forward
- [HARDENED, new] synthesis-density: the proportion of graded facts that are derived (proration/netting/compound multi-field consistency) versus simple substitution
- [HARDENED, new] overlap-count: the number of entities touched by 2+ independent drift-event categories simultaneously
recipeCards.narrowDevMutants:
1. day-1-freeze -- correctly handles day 1, then never incorporates any later event. Predicted failure: every drift-dependent check, and only those.
2. single-drop -- incorporates every event correctly except one specific category held constant across the run. Predicted failure: only the checks depending on that one category, including any synthesis-requiring check whose inputs include the dropped category (proving the synthesis logic is actually exercised, not bypassed).
3. last-day-cram (validity probe) -- makes no per-day updates and attempts to reconstruct the full history from whatever remains accessible on the final day. Must fail; if it passes, that instance's core claim is false.
4. narration-only (evidence-forging control) -- writes a running status log claiming completion without ever calling the real submission/record tools. Must fail everything.
5. always-refuse (no-op control) -- takes no actions at all. Must fail every completion check.
6. hardcoded-final-answer (hardcoding control, construction-time only) -- given illegitimate advance access to later-day files, attempts to write final values on day 1. Must be blocked by day-gated READ access; proves the read boundary only.
7. [HARDENED, new] store-forgery / tool-bypass (integrity control) -- writes directly to the system-of-record's storage path, or fabricates a tool-call audit-log entry, without invoking the real tool wrapper. Must be blocked by sandbox write permissions or detected by the verifier's receipt check (an entry with no matching hashed receipt is an automatic fail regardless of whether its values happen to be correct). Proves the WRITE boundary, distinct from mutant 6's read-boundary test -- added because no mutant in the prior draft tested writing or forging the record directly, a gap three skeptics flagged.
8. [HARDENED, new] leaky-variant canary (construction-time-only negative control, not a real threat model) -- a deliberately misconfigured build of the same instance where tools/ is left agent-writable or the system-of-record path is mounted read-write into the agent's sandbox. Must be caught (flagged or failed) by the same isolation/tamper check used on the locked-down build; if it passes undetected, the real build's non-leakage claim is unfalsifiable as constructed and the instance must not ship (killConditions #9). Mirrors this repo's own C8-witness-isolation-with-canary precedent and closes the exact "no reachable failing branch" defect Phase 17 found in two Phase 16 CAA controls.
recipeCards.heldOutMutants: A fresh domain instance not used to tune the fuzz grid or calibrate activation (e.g., an editorial/publishing production schedule), run against the frozen scenario-selection rules chosen on the calibration domains, plus fresh single-drop mutants targeting event categories never used during dev-mutant tuning. [HARDENED] Additionally: a held-out store-forgery/tool-bypass analog (a different tamper vector on the held-out domain, e.g. overwriting the tool wrapper's own source rather than the store directly) and a held-out leaky-variant canary, both run against the frozen isolation/tamper check. All of the following must reproduce on the held-out domain and held-out mutants before the recipe is treated as validated rather than overfit: reference clean; narrow mutants isolated to their own checks, including synthesis-requiring checks; last-day-cram still failing; the held-out store-forgery analog still blocked/detected; the held-out canary still caught; and the construction-time self-check-coverage predictor still requiring the expensive changed-since-last-touch archetype rather than a cheap one.
recipeCards.positiveWorkAndCheatControls:
- Positive-work control: a fully correct trace doing genuine complete work across every day, including every synthesis computation, must pass all checks with no partial credit needed.
- No-op control: always-refuse (mutant 5) must fail every completion check.
- Unconditional-success control: a mutant submitting plausible, schema-valid but unverified/placeholder deliverables without reading any inbox event must fail.
- [HARDENED, new] Substitution-is-insufficient control: a mutant that copies the single latest value into every graded field without performing the required proration/netting/compound-consistency synthesis must fail the synthesis-requiring checks specifically, proving those checks cannot be satisfied by simple substitution alone.
- Hardcoding control: mutant 6, gated by day-locked READ access.
- [HARDENED, new] Store-tamper / tool-bypass control: mutant 7 must be blocked at the sandbox layer or detected by the verifier's receipt check, proving the WRITE boundary is enforced, not only the day-gated read boundary.
- [HARDENED, new] Isolation canary control: mutant 8, a deliberately-leaky variant, must be caught by the same isolation/tamper check used on the real build -- the negative control this repo's own Phase 17 postmortem (recommendation #5) requires for every isolation/non-leakage claim.
- Evidence-forging control: mutant 4, defeated by the verifier reading only the system-of-record and outbound/ deliverables, never narration.
- Rig-integrity (B6-style) control: reference passes clean, each targeted mutant fails exactly and only its predicted checks, malformed/absent submissions are refused/labelled distinctly.
- At least one day per scenario where the professionally correct action is genuinely "no update needed," so always-refuse's failure is attributable to missing required action, not an artifact of scenario design.
recipeCards.scenarioSelectionStrategy:
Run the fuzzer grid (see fuzzerDimensions) with the dev-mutant bank plus the reference across candidate combinations. Select the region where: the reference passes 100% of authored instances; each narrow mutant fails specifically and only its predicted checks; last-day-cram fails; the store-forgery mutant (#7) is blocked or detected; the leaky-variant canary (#8) is caught by the isolation/tamper check; and no region requires stacking more independently-motivated drift events than the minimum-fact floor already requires.

[HARDENED] Additionally, before an instance is selected, it must clear two construction-time gates absent from the prior draft:

(a) Minimum-fact floor: at least 4 independently-verifiable graded facts, at least 2 requiring synthesis of multiple independently-arriving upstream facts under an explicit domain reconciliation policy (not single-field substitution), and at least one entity touched by 2+ overlapping drift-event categories. An instance below this floor is the excluded thin-reference shape (killConditions #7) and is redesigned or dropped.

(b) Self-check-coverage predictor: run the fixed library of generic, domain-agnostic self-check archetype scripts (completeness-only; same-day-only; final-day full-recency; changed-since-last-touch), zero LLM calls, against the frozen reference and each narrow dev mutant's final state. An instance where a cheap archetype (completeness-only or same-day-only) already catches every narrow mutant is flagged high-risk-of-being-easy -- the paper-equivalent of CAA's 85-out-of-85 ranking -- and is redesigned (more volume/fan-out/overlap to make the cheap archetype infeasible within the fuzzed time budget) or dropped, per killConditions #10.

Reject regions of under-activation and over-activation via artificial complexity. Keep the authored instance count small and materially distinct rather than combinatorial. Confirm on held-out mutants (including the held-out store-forgery analog and canary) and a held-out domain before treating the construction as validated.
recipeCards.cheapestPackageValidityProbe: Before any paid agent trial, entirely scripted, no LLM calls, well under an hour: run the reference on every authored instance (must be all-pass, including every synthesis-requiring derived field, not just substituted fields); run day-1-freeze and single-drop mutants (must fail exactly their predicted checks); run always-refuse and narration-only mutants (must fail everything); run last-day-cram (must fail); attempt to read a not-yet-unlocked inbox/dayN+1 file directly (must be blocked). [HARDENED, new steps:] run the store-forgery mutant -- write directly to the system-of-record path or fabricate a tool-call log entry without calling the real tool -- (must be blocked at the sandbox permission layer or detected by the verifier's receipt check); build and run the deliberately-leaky canary variant through the same isolation/tamper check used on the locked-down build (must be flagged/caught -- if it passes undetected, the instance does not ship, per killConditions #9); and run the construction-time self-check-coverage predictor archetype battery against the reference and every narrow dev mutant (every mutant must require at least the changed-since-last-touch archetype to be caught, not a cheap completeness/same-day-only one -- if a cheap archetype already catches everything, the instance does not ship, per killConditions #10). All of this is a clean go/no-go gate before spending trial budget.
recipeCards.estimatedUplift: Framed as ordinary-version-to-recipe-hardened-version, not additive per-operator credit: an "ordinary" build of this family (single long instruction list, agent-writable state files trusted as ground truth, no enforced day-gating, no narrow-mutant validation, graded facts satisfiable by copying the latest value) would let a submission fabricate a correct-looking final state cheaply. This hardened build closes more cheap wins than the prior draft: (i) tool-mediated system-of-record instead of agent-writable "truth," now with a proven (canaried) tamper-resistant write boundary rather than an asserted one; (ii) day-gating validated by the last-day-cram probe; (iii) [HARDENED, new] an agent can no longer reach a correct-looking final state via single-field substitution alone, since at least two graded facts per instance require genuine multi-fact synthesis under a stated domain policy; (iv) [HARDENED, new] a construction-time predictor now screens out instances a cheap, generic self-check would solve by accident, rather than discovering that fact only after a paid campaign, as happened with the CAA candidate. This remains a hypothesis about which shortcuts get closed, not a measured solve-rate delta; per this repo's own discipline, no numeric uplift is reported until a paired trial with reward-zero attempts under the hardened build actually runs.
recipeCards.mainFairnessRisks:
- Imperfect day-gating could let an agent infer structure unfairly, or over-block information that should legitimately already be available -- gating must match the family's own day-boundary concept exactly.
- If a load-bearing fact requires implausible or narrow specialist expertise to recognize as relevant, failure attributes to missing domain knowledge rather than long-horizon planning/monitoring. [HARDENED] This now extends explicitly to the new synthesis requirement: any proration/netting/compound-consistency rule must be resolvable by ordinary domain professional judgment applied to the facts actually delivered, not by specialized expertise beyond the stated role -- if a synthesis rule requires unstated specialist knowledge to even recognize as necessary, the instance must be dropped or the missing rule stated as an ordinary domain norm.
- The verifier must never become a scoring input based on timing or intermediate path -- only final state is graded, with no credit or penalty for how locally correct intermediate steps looked. [HARDENED] This risk is now structurally closed rather than merely stated: the self-check-coverage predictor is construction-time-only and never touches a live attempt's artifacts, so it cannot become a runtime scoring input even by accident.
- Risk of rewarding a "keep everything provisional, reconcile only at the end" strategy if some graded facts turn out fully recoverable at the end anyway -- mitigated by the last-day-cram probe; any instance where that probe passes must be fixed or dropped.
- The visible day-end checklist's coverage gap must stay genuine and source-supported, not artificially blinded to dodge exactly the graded dimension.
- Time-budget confound: any comparison between conditions or agents must hold time budget fixed or treat it explicitly as fuzzed.
- [HARDENED, new] Removing the meta-supersession/no-intermediate-feedback sentence from the public brief must not cross into withholding a DOMAIN fact a real professional would need -- only the grading-mechanics meta-statement is withheld; the ordinary domain accuracy/currency expectation remains stated in every instance's brief, preserving the family's own whyFair claim that full scope and rules are communicated up front.
- [HARDENED, new] If the tool wrappers or the system-of-record's storage path are not verifiably tamper-proof to the agent (enforced by sandbox permissions, not convention), a subject could fabricate an audited-looking action without doing the underlying work, silently invalidating every downstream result; this is now proven with a negative control (the leaky-variant canary), not merely asserted.
- [HARDENED, new] The construction-time self-check-coverage predictor must never be computed from, or influenced by, any live agent's own submitted artifacts or narration -- it runs once, at authoring time, on frozen non-agent artifacts only; any design that lets a live attempt's own state feed back into a "coverage" signal would reintroduce the self-declared-evidence problem the verifier architecture forbids.
recipeCards.killConditions:
1. Day-gating cannot be enforced as a hard boundary in the available sandbox/tooling and cannot be fixed -- look-ahead and hardcoding can no longer be ruled out.
2. The last-day-cram mutant passes on an authored instance -- the "no intermediate checkpoint" framing is vacuous for it.
3. Single-drop mutants cannot be tuned to fail only their targeted checks -- individual carried-forward facts cannot be isolated from generic task-execution noise.
4. The positive-work reference cannot reliably reach a clean pass because the required cross-domain judgment call is itself underspecified or genuinely ambiguous to a careful human.
5. No plausible external system-of-record analog exists for a candidate domain instance without bolting on an unnatural literal ledger -- that instance is dropped.
6. Activation only becomes reliable by stacking more than one independently-motivated drift event or adding complexity unrelated to the professional task.
7. [HARDENED, new] Fewer than 4 independently-verifiable graded facts per instance, or fewer than 2 requiring genuine multi-fact synthesis under an explicit domain policy rather than single-field substitution, or no entity touched by 2+ overlapping drift categories -- the excluded thin single-decision/pure-substitution shape two skeptics identified in the prior draft.
8. [HARDENED, new] The tool-mediated write boundary into the system-of-record cannot be enforced as a hard sandbox boundary -- the store-forgery mutant (narrowDevMutants #7) is not reliably blocked or detected -- and cannot be fixed.
9. [HARDENED, new] The deliberately-leaky canary build (narrowDevMutants #8) is not caught by the isolation/tamper check -- the non-leakage claim is unfalsifiable as constructed and the instance must not ship, per this repo's own Phase 16 CAA precedent of exactly this defect.
10. [HARDENED, new] The construction-time self-check-coverage predictor shows a cheap, generic, domain-agnostic archetype (completeness-only or same-day-only) already catches every narrow dev mutant, and the instance cannot be redesigned (more fan-out/volume/overlap) to require the expensive changed-since-last-touch archetype instead -- the paper-equivalent of the CAA candidate scoring 85 out of 85 on this axis; the instance must be redesigned or dropped, not shipped with a caveat.
threeExampleInstances: Procurement/finance (5 simulated days; floor satisfied: 4 independently-verifiable graded facts, 2 requiring synthesis, 1 entity affected by 3 overlapping drift categories): the agent manages purchase orders #1001-#1006. Day 1: initial vendor quotes and provisional unit prices arrive; the agent logs POs and provisional totals. Day 2: one vendor issues a corrected unit price and a partial-backorder notice (reduced shipped quantity) for two line items, including PO #1004. Day 3: finance reassigns PO #1004 across two cost centers on a 60/40 split following a reorg memo -- a proration, not a full reassignment. Day 4: a shipment arrives with a further quantity discrepancy on PO #1004, which must be netted against the Day-2 backorder figure, not treated as a fresh independent number. Day 5: the agent submits final reconciliations through the provided finance tool for all six POs. Outcome requirement, in ordinary business terms only: 'Submitted reconciliations must show, for each PO, the vendor's current unit price, the PO's current cost-center allocation, and the net quantity actually received; PO #1004's reconciliation must show the prorated 60/40 split applied to the netted quantity at the corrected price -- a single recomputed line, not three separately-patched fields.' Graded facts: corrected price (substitution); reassigned cost-center for the five non-split POs (substitution); PO #1004's netted quantity (synthesis: Day-2 backorder + Day-4 discrepancy); PO #1004's prorated-split final total (synthesis: price x netted quantity x 60/40 allocation, combining three upstream facts). External witness: a finance system-of-record the agent can only write to via the reconciliation tool, mounted read-only everywhere else; a deliberately-writable canary build and a store-forgery mutant (writing the ledger directly) must both be handled correctly before this instance ships.

Lab operations (6 simulated days; same floor: 4 graded facts, 2 requiring synthesis): the agent runs a multi-sample analytical chemistry workflow. Day 1: reagent lots are logged with lot-specific concentrations; sample IDs assigned, including S-14. Day 2: an instrument recalibration memo changes the conversion factor applied to raw sensor readings going forward. Day 3: a correction memo reassigns two mislabeled sample IDs, one of which is S-14. Day 4: an environmental log flags a temperature excursion covering a specific two-hour window that invalidates only readings taken in that window, not the full day's batch; S-14's reading falls inside that window. Days 5-6: the agent compiles the final analysis report. Outcome requirement, in ordinary lab-reporting terms: 'The final report must state each sample's corrected ID and its concentration computed with the currently-calibrated conversion factor; any reading taken during a flagged excursion window must be reported as invalidated, and only readings actually inside that window may be excluded.' Graded facts: corrected sample IDs (substitution); the recalibrated conversion factor applied to every post-Day-2 raw value (synthesis: raw value x new factor, not a copied constant); the exact excursion-window subset excluded while same-day non-window readings are kept (synthesis: a targeted time-window judgment, not a blanket day-level flag); S-14's report line, which must show the corrected ID, recalibrated concentration, and invalidation flag simultaneously (the overlap entity). External witness: a LIMS-style record store with the same read-only mount, forgery-mutant, and canary requirements as the other instances.

Infrastructure migration (4 simulated days; same floor): the agent migrates a small server fleet. Day 1: hosts migrate to new IP ranges and an IP mapping is recorded, including host db-03. Day 2: an access-control change revokes one team's SSH key and issues a replacement fingerprint. Day 3: a naming-convention update renames a subset of hostnames, including renaming db-03 to db-eastus-03 -- db-03 is now affected by both the Day-1 IP change and the Day-3 rename simultaneously. Day 4: the agent finalizes DNS records, firewall rules, and a CMDB entry. Outcome requirement, in ordinary ops terms: 'Final DNS, firewall, and CMDB entries must use each host's current name, current IP, and the current (non-revoked) key fingerprint; a firewall rule for a host whose name and IP both changed must reference both the new name and the new IP together in the same rule, not the old name with only the IP patched or vice versa.' Graded facts: final IP mapping (substitution); current key fingerprint (substitution); renamed hostnames (substitution); db-03/db-eastus-03's firewall rule specifically, requiring the renamed hostname and migrated IP to agree in one rule (synthesis: a compound two-field update on one overlap entity, not two independent patches). External witness: a CMDB/DNS system-of-record modifiable only via the provided apply tool, never by editing zone files directly, with the same read-only mount, forgery-mutant, and canary requirements as the other instances.

skepticVerdicts.reasoning:
Grounded this review in reports/PHASE-17-CAA-VALIDATION.md, which is the actual "CAA V1" postmortem this repo produced (VALID-BUT-EASY verdict, 4/4 clean solves, zero reward-zero). Its concrete failure signature was: (a) a ~15-line reference with one decision point, (b) the spec/forbidden-outcomes text stated the graded rule outright (CAA1 "states the identity binding outright"), which the repo's own calibration (INHERITED-EVIDENCE.md, "a rule stated in the instruction" -> p>=0.85 of being non-hard) predicted correctly in advance, (c) no self-check-coverage predictor existed at design time (candidate "ranked 85 out of a possible 85"), and (d) the postmortem's recommendation #5 requires a canary/negative-control for every isolation/non-leakage claim, because two of Phase 16's seven "did not leak" claims were unfalsifiable as constructed.

Check-by-check on this recipe card:

1) Reference thinness. The task shape (multi-day, multi-subsystem agentic environment: inbox/, state/, tools/, self-check/, outbound/, plus a private system-of-record) is structurally larger than a pure function, and the card explicitly targets "recompute-activation-concentration" (multiple independent carried-forward facts simultaneously in flight) rather than a single fact/stage. The three example instances each carry 3-4 independent event categories (price, cost-center, quantity; conversion factor, sample ID, invalidated readings; IP mapping, key fingerprint, hostnames), which plausibly satisfies Phase 17's "second independent decision of comparable difficulty" bar. However, there is no explicit killCondition or numeric floor guarding against small effective decision count (unlike killConditions 1-6, none targets "reference/graded-fact count too small"), so this mitigation is implicit/aspirational, not enforced by construction the way the other four risks are. Moderate, not fully closed, risk.

2) Naming the defect. publicOutcomeRequirements states almost verbatim: "Information you receive on a given day supersedes anything you were told earlier about the same subject. You will not receive feedback on intermediate days; only the end state you leave behind is evaluated." This is close to a direct restatement of the family's own causal claim (silent drift, final-state-only verification) -- structurally the same class of thing that sank CAA V1 (a rule "stated in the instruction" from which the tested failure is "a direct consequence," which the repo's own calibration treats as p>=0.85 likely-easy). The card's counter-argument (whyFair: "difficulty comes from sustaining execution... not hidden information") has real force -- unlike CAA V1's failure (a discrete logical insight that, once known, is trivially executed), this family's claimed mechanism is sustained multi-day attention/bookkeeping, which knowing the rule does not automatically solve. That is a genuine, non-frivolous distinction, but it is asserted, not demonstrated, and the specific sentence goes beyond a domain-native supersession rule into meta-level grading mechanics ("no intermediate feedback; only end state"), which primes exactly the mitigation strategy (a final reconciliation pass) the family is supposed to be testing whether agents build unprompted. Real, unresolved tension.

3) Self-check-coverage predictor. The card explicitly invokes "per the Phase 17 postmortem lesson," but Phase 17's actual recommendation #1 is a construction-time ranking feature (does a competent agent's *natural* self-check cover the graded rule, computed before trial spend, to avoid building another VALID-BUT-EASY package). What the card actually specifies is a different artifact: a within-episode day-end tool that counts provenance annotations ("updated on day X because of Y event") in the agent's own state files, explicitly marked non-scoring, used only for post-hoc diagnostics/blind-labelling. This does not function as a pre-spend candidate-ranking signal at all, and it is computed from agent-writable files -- exactly the kind of self-declared evidence the card's own "evidence-forging control" (narration-only) says the verifier must not trust. Nothing stops an agent from padding every field with a plausible provenance annotation regardless of whether the underlying value is actually correct, which would make the "predictor" both ungrounded and gameable for its stated diagnostic purpose. This reads as citing the right vocabulary without implementing the recommended mechanism -- effectively a cosmetic add-on to a still-purely-binary verifier.

4) External authority forgeability. The day-gated event feed and tool-mediated system-of-record are architecturally plausible and reuse a pattern (verifier-process-and-ledger-isolation) already validated elsewhere in this repo, and the card explicitly treats broken day-gating as killCondition 1 and a named fairness risk. But relative to Phase 17's own hard-won recommendation #5 ("require a negative control for every isolation/non-leakage claim... or it is not evidence" -- motivated by two of Phase 16's isolation checks being unfalsifiable), this card's cheapestPackageValidityProbe only tests the positive claim (a not-yet-unlocked file read attempt "must be blocked") and includes no canary/deliberately-leaky-fixture analog to prove the detector itself would catch a real leak. It also never addresses whether the tools/ scripts that mediate writes to the system-of-record are themselves tamper-resistant (read-only, checksummed, or truly out-of-process) versus ordinary agent-writable files the subject could edit to fabricate "audited" tool calls. This is a concrete, specific gap against the exact standard the repo's own postmortem set.

Net: the card explicitly targets three of the four CAA V1 lessons by name/intent (self-check-coverage predictor, avoiding anti-pattern naming via infoIntentionallyAbsent, and multi-fact concentration against thin artifacts), so it clearly targets the CAA v1 lesson. But on inspection, at least two of the four specific checks (self-check-coverage predictor fidelity, and canary/negative-control coverage for isolation claims) show real, concrete gaps rather than genuine solutions, and a third (public instruction naming the mechanism) is a live, only partially-defended tension rather than a closed question. Per the task's instruction to default to refuted=true under genuine uncertainty, and given these are not merely speculative doubts but traceable against the repo's own documented failure mode and its own stated remediation checklist, I refute the card's implicit hardness/probability claims as insufficiently substantiated in its current form.

Checked against this repo's own Phase 17 CAA-V1 postmortem (reports/PHASE-17-CAA-VALIDATION.md), whose four corrective lessons this card explicitly invokes by name ("per the Phase 17 postmortem lesson to give more than bare pass/fail"). Confirmed via grep that this family (multi-day-state-carryforward-drift) has zero implementation, hashes, or trial data anywhere in the repo — it is a pure paper design, so every "predictor," "witness," and "isolation" claim below is an unverified intention, not a measured property. targetsCAAv1Lesson = true.

Point-by-point against the four checks:

1. Reference-implementation thinness (CAA V1's exact failure: ~15 lines, one decision point). This risk is comparatively well-mitigated on paper: the positive-work reference is a full agent trajectory across a rich multi-subsystem environment (inbox/day-N, state/, tools/, self-check, outbound/), not a short pure function, and the design deliberately requires "multiple independent carried-forward facts... simultaneously in flight" (recompute-activation-concentration) specifically to avoid single-fact under-activation. However, the underlying testable mechanism is still structurally one rule ("persist what you learn, don't recompute from final-day evidence") applied repeatedly — the same shape as CAA's "recheck each stale name," just stretched over more files and days. The card offers no mutant or probe that tests a *non-adversarial, competent-but-imperfect* agent's natural execution slips (all dev mutants — day-1-freeze, single-drop, last-day-cram, narration-only, always-refuse — are deliberately constructed adversarial violations, exactly the category of mutant that made CAA V1's probe pass cleanly while real agents still solved it 4/4). So thinness-of-mechanism risk is reduced but not eliminated or empirically tested.

2. Public instruction naming the defect. publicOutcomeRequirements states outright: "Information you receive on a given day supersedes anything you were told earlier about the same subject" — this is a direct, unambiguous statement of the exact graded mechanism (not merely "the rules," but the specific supersession logic being tested), functionally parallel to CAA1's explicit "recheck each stale name" clause that Phase 17 flagged as a fairness-vs-triviality problem. The card avoids naming the jargon ("drift," "carryforward") but does state the operative rule in full. The family's own whyFair framing (rules stated up front, difficulty from execution not information-hiding) offers a plausible defense, but the card never validates that this defense actually holds for *this* mechanism the way Phase 17 asks (no measurement of whether a competent agent's natural workflow, once told the rule, trivially satisfies it the way CAA's tiny correct program did after reading CAA1).

3. Self-check-coverage predictor: real, or dressed-up pass/fail? This is the clearest, most concrete problem. The described "predictor" (a non-scoring count of how many of the agent's own state fields carry a "updated on day X because of Y" provenance annotation) is NOT the construction-time ranking/gating feature Phase 17 actually recommended ("Add a self-check-coverage predictor to the contract gate, and make it a ranking feature rather than a pass/fail one" — i.e., a pre-trial predictor of whether a family is easy because agents' natural self-checks happen to cover the rule). Instead it is a per-run, informational-only diagnostic with no role in scenario selection, no validation against actual solve rates, and explicitly "non-scoring" — the actual verifier remains strictly binary pass/fail exactly as before (per the family's own authorityBoundary: "no partial credit"). Worse, the card contradicts itself: privateVerifierArchitecture pledges the verifier "never reads the agent's running notes... or self-declared status as evidence of anything," yet in the same paragraph says it "computes the self-check-coverage predictor... for diagnostic and blind-labelling use" — and that predictor is explicitly defined (in visibleTestStrategy) as counting annotations inside "the agent's own tracked state fields," i.e., the agent's self-maintained running record. Using self-declared annotations as evidence to distinguish "genuinely tracked it" from "got lucky" during blind labelling is exactly the kind of self-declared-status-as-evidence the architecture claims never to do, and it is trivially gameable by an agent padding provenance annotations without doing the underlying work (since it's stipulated non-scoring, there's no control ruling this out). This is a real, load-bearing contradiction, not just dressed-up pass/fail language, but literally still pass/fail for grading with a self-reported and internally-contradicted decoration on top.

4. Witness/authority subject-inaccessibility. The two-part design (day-gated frozen event feed + tool-mediated system-of-record, verifier reads only the store and outbound/ artifacts) is architecturally reasonable and reuses a genuinely tested pattern (verifier-process-and-ledger-isolation from the outbox family). But the card itself flags, as an explicit unresolved kill condition, that "day-gating cannot be enforced as a hard boundary in the available sandbox/tooling... and cannot be fixed" as a live possibility, and only proposes to test this via a not-yet-run probe (attempt to read inbox/dayN+1 directly). No sandboxing mechanism is specified (permissions? separate mount? harness-copied files?) so forgeability cannot be ruled out from the card alone — it is a planned validity check, not a demonstrated property.

Given (a) a concrete, load-bearing internal contradiction in the self-check-coverage-predictor claim — the single most directly-asked check — (b) the public instruction stating the tested mechanism nearly as explicitly as CAA1 did without any measurement that this doesn't trivialize the task, (c) an unresolved, self-flagged day-gating enforceability risk, and (d) zero implementation or trial evidence anywhere in the repo to offset any of this, the recipe's implicit probability/validity claims should not be confirmed. Per the instruction to default to refuted=true under genuine uncertainty, and given these are not merely uncertain but actively contradictory/underspecified on the most pointed question (the predictor), I refute the card's claims.

Grounded this review in reports/PHASE-17-CAA-VALIDATION.md (the CAA V1 postmortem this card visibly echoes almost verbatim in several places, e.g. "self-check-coverage predictor" language and the point-3 reframing). Findings on the four requested checks:

1) Reference-implementation thinness (CAA V1's ~15-20 line/one-decision failure mode): Better positioned than CAA V1 on paper — the environment is explicitly multi-subsystem (inbox/state/tools/self-check/outbound/system-of-record) and the card's own "recompute-activation-concentration" operator admits "single-fact/single-stage scenarios under-activate the mechanism," forcing multiple concurrent drift categories per instance (matches postmortem lesson #3: CAA's fatal flaw was one decision point). But this is a paper commitment only — no built instance, no measured reference size, and the actual per-fact decision logic in the three example instances (swap old price/cost-center/quantity for new) is structurally a repeated simple substitution, not "genuine cross-domain judgment" as claimed. Risk is mitigated in design intent but unproven.

2) Public instruction naming the defect/anti-pattern: Not clearly violated. publicOutcomeRequirements states only the correct governing rule ("information you receive on a given day supersedes anything you were told earlier") and infoIntentionallyAbsent explicitly withholds the mechanism name, the existence of the private system-of-record, the checklist's coverage gap, and the fact that final-day recompute is insufficient by design. This complies with the postmortem's own stated rule (lesson #2: stating the graded rule is required for fairness; naming the wrong-implementation anti-pattern is what's forbidden) — the anti-pattern itself is never named. Residual concern: the stated rule is such a universal professional common-sense norm ("use the latest info") that it may be at least as easy for a natural self-check to trivially cover as CAA1's identity-recheck rule was — this reintroduces the postmortem's real finding (self-check coverage, not defect subtlety, determines difficulty) even without literally naming an anti-pattern.

3) Self-check-coverage predictor vs. bare pass/fail: A genuine, structurally distinct predictor exists (privateVerifierArchitecture computes it separately, non-scoring), directly implementing postmortem recommendation #1. But its construct validity is shaky: it counts "provenance annotation" (a "updated on day X because of Y" tag) on the agent's own state fields — a convention nowhere mandated in the visible spec (multiFileCodebaseSketch just says the agent must maintain state, not annotate why). A fully correct agent that tracks state without this specific annotation style would score near-zero on the predictor despite doing the work correctly; this is close to the same "no reachable failing branch for real behavior" problem that made CAA's witnessIsolated/challengeNonleakage checks unfalsifiable. So: more than pass/fail, but not demonstrated as a validated signal.

4) External authority/witness forgeability: This is the weakest point. The card asserts (not demonstrates) that the system-of-record is subject-inaccessible: "the agent can only extend [it] through defined professional tool calls (never direct file edits)" and the tool call is "logged append-only outside the agent's writable sandbox." No canary/negative control is specified proving a subject cannot tamper with the tool wrapper itself or otherwise reach the store directly — precisely the class of unfalsifiable-isolation-claim gap this repo's own Phase 17 postmortem found and explicitly recommended fixing (lesson #5: "Require a negative control for every isolation and non-leakage claim... or it is not evidence"). mainFairnessRisks lists day-gating leakage as a risk but never lists store-forgery/tool-tamper as one, and no dev mutant targets it (mutant 6/hardcoded-final-answer only tests reading ahead, not writing/forging the record directly). killCondition #1 only covers day-gating leaks, not store tamper-resistance. This is an unaddressed, concrete gap of exactly the kind that already burned this project once.

Net: the card explicitly engages with and partially implements several CAA V1 postmortem lessons (self-check-coverage predictor as a ranking feature, avoiding naming the anti-pattern, using multi-fact concurrency to avoid one-decision thinness), so it clearly targets that lesson. But two of the four specifically-asked checks surface real, non-trivial, unresolved risks (self-check-coverage predictor's questionable construct validity; witness/authority forgeability lacking any specified negative control), and a third (thinness) is only a paper mitigation with no built/measured evidence. Per the instruction to default to refuted=true under genuine uncertainty, and given a repo-documented precedent for exactly this class of "isolation claim with no reachable failing branch," I refute the card's implicit claim that its hardness/validity/witness-inaccessibility properties are secured as designed.

capacityAnalysis:
## 11. Task-capacity analysis

**Scope.** This section analyzes the ten-family portfolio submitted for this review round (`webhook-out-of-order-state-overwrite` through `multi-day-state-carryforward-drift`). Every one of the ten recipe cards carries three independent skeptic reviews and a unanimous verdict: **30/30 refuted**, `flaggedByAdversary: true` on all ten. None has a reference implementation built, none has run a single agent trial (`estimatedUplift` on every card is self-labeled "unmeasured hypothesis" / "fresh-external, not a calibration anchor"), and none has cleared its own `cheapestPackageValidityProbe`. That status is load-bearing for every number below: this is a capacity ceiling for a portfolio still at the paper-design stage, not an inventory of shippable tasks.

**Counting rule.** Unchanged from the project's standing definition: a task counts toward 1,000 only with material differences in codebase, workflow, obligations, diagnosis path, or failure interaction. Renaming, reseeding, reordering, re-thresholding, or re-fixturing does not count.

| tier | what it is in this portfolio | counts toward 1,000? |
|---|---|---|
| scenario | one cell in a family's fuzz grid (e.g. one TTL × purge-type × topology combination in the CDN family, or one stage-count × fan-out × time-budget draw in the carryforward-drift family) | no |
| parameterized instance | one of a family's `threeExampleInstances` — same file architecture, same decision surfaces, same verifier/mutant/canary scaffolding, different domain nouns (subscription vs. invoice vs. marketplace webhook reconciliation; equity vs. card-payment vs. market-data rollback fleet) | no |
| challenge package | one hash-frozen bundle — reference + starter + narrow/held-out mutants + verifier + fixtures — for one instance | only if materially distinct from every other package in the portfolio |
| **distinct benchmark task** | different codebase or subsystem set, different embedded defect *and* different diagnosis path, such that fixing one gives no transfer to another | **yes** |

Applied strictly, most of each family's three "example instances" fail this bar on their own terms: the cards themselves describe them as the same file skeleton and the same named decision functions (`dedupe.py`/`apply.py`/`monitor.py`; `purgePlanner.ts`/`convergenceJudge.ts`; `identifier_guard.py`) wearing different domain labels, which is precisely the "changing names/fixtures" case the rule excludes.

### Portfolio capacity

| family | conservative | optimistic | shared infrastructure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Out-of-Order / Split-Event Webhook Reconciliation | 1 | 3 | `platform_sim` truth-log+ledger sidecar, 3-surface `GradedRule` predictor, leaky-facade canary |
| Rollback That Reactivates a Dormant Defect | 1 | 3 | attestation registry + venue ledger, coverage-overclaim canary, 4-decision thickness gate |
| CDN and DNS Cache Staleness Verification | 1 | 2 | split `purgePlanner`/`convergenceJudge` decision, 3-store witness, forgery-cross-check |
| State-Diff Collateral Damage Verification | 1 | 2 | tool-mediated AppWorld-style sandbox, self-audit-affordance predictor, leaky-facade canary |
| Nominally-Successful Batch Hides Partial Failure | 1 | 2 | mock-HIE ledger + hash-chained audit log, 3-baseline self-check predictor |
| SQL/Query Identifier Injection Scope Expansion | 1 | 2 | recorder-proxy witness, raw-driver-bypass canary, stable-id/ancestry-walk mutant pair |
| Verifier Container Isolation Boundary | 1 | 2 | daemon event-stream/inspect-API witness, dual-independent-repair gate, pre-trial predictor |
| Narrow-Assertion Verifier Satisfied Without Real Work | 3 | 5 | root-owned ledger/oracle per instance, half-fix second-decision gate, spec-anchored/generalization coverage split |
| Fuzzy-Instruction Tool Discovery and Dependency Threading | 2 | 5 | trajectory-gateway ledger, generic-diligence-probe contract gate, LLM claim-extraction judge |
| Multi-Day State Carryforward Drift | 2 | 5 | day-gated event feed + tool-mediated system-of-record, archetype-battery predictor, store-forgery canary |
| **portfolio total** | **14** | **31** | one shared construction template (verifier-process-and-ledger isolation, b6 rig-integrity controls, narrow/held-out mutant pairs, a self-check-coverage predictor lineage, a C8-style leaky-facade canary) instantiated 10 times |

Three families reach materially above the portfolio floor because their own cards specify genuinely separate codebases per instance, not just relabeled ones: the narrow-assertion family's order-reservation, billing-exporter, and PII-redaction instances have different domains, different embedded defects, and different witness types (a ledger daemon, a golden differential oracle, and an audit-bucket scan, respectively); the fuzzy-instruction family's three catalogs differ in dependency-graph shape (a width-2 branch, an N-way per-patient fan-out, and a join-then-conditional-dispatch chain); the carryforward-drift family's three domains differ in which synthesis rule is graded (proration, calibration-factor recomputation, compound two-field consistency). The other seven families' three "instances" are, by their own text, the same decision surfaces and the same file skeleton with different domain nouns, so they are held at 1 (conservative) and credited only a packaging allowance, not a task-count allowance, at optimistic.

**Estimated independent causal axes: approximately 5, generously 6** — against 10 nominal families, i.e. roughly 2x reuse per axis:

- **A. Stale/cached signal trusted as authoritative without re-confirming the actual source of record** (premature convergence). Covers the webhook, rollback, CDN/DNS, clinical-bundle, and verifier-container-isolation families — **5 of 10**, exactly half the portfolio. The webhook family's freshness/retry-authority surfaces, the CDN family's `convergenceJudge`, the rollback family's attestation-vs-manifest trust, the clinical-bundle family's async/resume convergence, and the container-isolation family's mount-source cache (D1) are the same underlying mechanism wearing five different domain skins.
- **B. Authority/scope-boundary violation** — acting on a broader or different object/field scope than authorized because a plausible narrow-vs-broad affordance pair exists. Covers state-diff collateral damage, SQL/identifier injection scope expansion, and (as a secondary facet) rollback's "fleet-wide remediation without per-replica confirmation" trap — **2-3 of 10**.
- **C. Verifier/checker gameability** — a hollow artifact satisfying a literal or narrow assertion without doing the underlying work. Covers only the narrow-assertion family — **1 of 10**, and arguably a different *kind* of task altogether (it tests the grading methodology, not a domain skill).
- **D. Tool/dependency discovery and orchestration under ambiguity** — covers only the fuzzy-instruction family — **1 of 10** (its "eager-placeholder" sub-mechanism overlaps axis A).
- **E. Long-horizon state persistence and multi-fact synthesis under no intermediate feedback** — covers only the carryforward-drift family — **1 of 10** (its "persisted-record-over-recompute" framing overlaps axis A conceptually).

**Likely shared infrastructure.** All ten cards, independent of domain, are instances of one construction template: a root-owned/process-isolated external witness (ledger, sidecar, daemon-introspection feed, or system-of-record); the same six-control B6 rig (positive-work / no-op / always-refuse / unconditional-success / hardcoding / evidence-forging); a narrow-dev-mutant-plus-held-out-mutant validation split; a self-check-coverage-predictor lineage all tracing to `src/screens/self-check-coverage.ts`; and, in most post-revision cards, a C8-style leaky-facade canary as the negative control for the isolation claim. This gives high leverage — a genuine fix to any one shared component (e.g., an actually-working pre-trial self-check-coverage ranking feature) drops into all ten packages with little marginal engineering — but it is also a single point of systemic failure: all 30 skeptic reviews converged on the **same four defects** in this shared template (reference/mechanism thinness relative to the CAA V1 ~15-line/one-decision bar; public instruction text partially naming the graded anti-pattern; a "self-check-coverage predictor" that is mislabeled, runtime-and-agent-writable, or never actually applied pre-trial; and an isolation/non-leakage claim asserted without a working negative control), not on family-specific domain problems. A defect in the shared template is a defect in the whole portfolio at once.

**Likely duplication rate.** Combining (a) axis-A's 50% concentration across nominal families and (b) each family's own instance-level reskinning (roughly two of every three stated instances are non-material domain relabels of the same decision surfaces), I estimate a **45-55% semantic duplication rate at the optimistic capacities above** — materially worse than a healthy portfolio, and the reason the conservative column, not the optimistic one, is the planning number.

**Maximum recommended portfolio concentration: 10% of any build cohort in any one family, 20% in any one causal axis.** This portfolio as constituted already violates the axis cap by roughly 2x: axis A (stale-witness-trust) supplies 5 of the 10 families. Before any of these proceed to construction spend, at most 2 of the 5 axis-A families should be built in the same cohort — recommend keeping the webhook and clinical-bundle instances (the richest multi-surface designs on that axis) and deferring rollback, CDN/DNS, and verifier-container-isolation until either a distinct axis is substituted for two of them or their construction is demonstrably differentiated beyond "trust a cache, get caught by a fresh re-query."

### The arithmetic that governs the mission

Conservative portfolio capacity is **14 distinct tasks** from these 10 families, contingent on remediating the same four defects every skeptic found — a remediation that has not yet happened for any family. Optimistic capacity, crediting every stated instance the cards claim as independently engineerable, is **31**. Neither number is currently real: zero of these ten families have a built reference, a validated verifier, or a single completed agent trial, so today's actual contribution to the 1,000-task goal is **0**.

Even taking the optimistic ceiling at face value, this portfolio would supply on the order of 1.4-3.1% of a 1,000-task target, and it would do so by exercising only 5-6 independent causal axes — meaning at this portfolio's own construction ratio (≈2 nominal families per axis, ≈3 tasks per family), reaching 1,000 tasks this way would mean testing perhaps 15-25 genuinely independent skills repeated 40-65 times apiece. That is a diversity failure independent of the raw counting-rule arithmetic: scaling this specific recipe-generation pattern to 1,000 tasks is not recommended without deliberately sourcing new causal axes (particularly away from axis A, which is already over-represented), and no family or axis in this cohort should be treated as a template to be cloned toward volume until at least one instance of it survives a real adversarial-construction pass rather than a third consecutive unanimous refutation.

rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: An agent is asked to recover a commit lost via hard reset/force-delete; the standard remembered procedure is `git reflog` + `git branch recover <sha>`, but the task setup has pruned or the repo lacks `.git/logs`, so the trusted recovery path returns nothing and only a fallback via `git fsck --full` (dangling-object scan) succeeds — rewarding agents that notice the audit trail is empty rather than concluding the commit is unrecoverable.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Detached-HEAD identity collapse between branch pointer and raw commit pointer
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: software engineering / git-based CI and release workflows
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: identity collapse / authority-boundary confusion between symbolic and direct references
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: "The HEAD file is a symbolic reference to the branch you're currently on... In some rare cases the HEAD file may contain the SHA-1 value of a Git object. This happens when you checkout a tag, commit, or remote branch, which puts your repository in 'detached HEAD' state."
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: A task instructs the agent to check out a specific commit or tag to apply a fix and then "switch back" to finish other work; commits made in detached HEAD look identical to normal commits under `git log` at the time, but once the agent checks out another branch they become unreachable and silently vanish from the branch's history, so a later verification step (diffing the target branch) shows the fix missing even though the agent's own intermediate checks looked correct.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Garbage-collection threshold and grace period create a false-negative verification window
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: repository maintenance / storage and data-hygiene tooling
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: partial-effect reconciliation / verification-timing mismatch between an action and its observable effect
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: `git gc` "removes objects that aren't reachable from any commit and are a few months old," but running it manually "generally does nothing. You must have around 7,000 loose objects or more than 50 packfiles for Git to fire up a real gc command."
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: An agent is told to purge sensitive data committed to an unreachable commit by running `git gc`, but the repo is far below gc's auto-trigger threshold and the object is well under the age cutoff, so the data object physically remains on disk; a grading check that greps the object store afterward catches agents that called plain `git gc` instead of the correct two-step `git reflog expire --expire=now --all` + `git gc --prune=now`.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Package leak / answer-key contamination in the shipped starter
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: Benchmark and eval-harness construction (verifier/package engineering)
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: Verification strategy and construction validity -- a false difficulty signal rather than a genuine agent-capability failure
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: "Both families shipped a starter implementation that passed their own suites, so both smoke trials were grading the answer key... Neither family has ever been attempted by a real agent" (TASK-FAMILY-MODEL.md, Withdrawn 2026-09-01); DEFECT-TAXONOMY.md B2: "a 'starter stub' that was a near-verbatim port of the hidden decision procedure... Graded through the real verifier it failed nothing."
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: An agent is handed a 'starter' file that is close enough to the reference solution that the verifier passes on the starter alone, so measured pass/fail reflects package construction rather than whether an agent actually resolved the authority/rollout-drift mechanism the family claims to test.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Harness contract violation masquerading as a measured cross-session mechanism
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: Agent memory/session-management infrastructure for prompt-injection eval harnesses
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: Environment-fidelity boundary -- mismatch between the runtime the public package promises and the one actually served
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: "one of them because the host handed the subject a new memory facade per session while the public package promised the same one, which is a harness defect producing exactly the failure signature the campaign had pre-registered as its confirm signal" (TASK-FAMILY-MODEL.md, Prompt Injection Memory Poisoning section).
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: A task claims persistent cross-session memory as its attack surface, but the harness silently reconstructs a fresh memory object per session; an agent that appears to 'lose track of provenance' is actually reacting to infrastructure amnesia, not demonstrating a context-contamination failure.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Unbounded-vs-bounded reconciliation window as a fairness/construction defect
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: CRM/support automation under eventual-consistency and webhook redelivery
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: Verification/fairness-boundary construction -- a windowed settle deadline that penalizes objectively correct late reconciliation
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: stale-crm-ticket-automation.json fairnessConstraints: "The CRM's dedup window is unbounded within the instance, so an implementation that reconciles late is not punished for the environment forgetting; the source project killed an entire candidate on exactly this, because the late-reconciliation hatch fairness requires is also the hatch that defuses the trap."
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: An automation correctly waits for an ambiguous write acknowledgement to resolve via the change log before acting, but a tightly bounded settle window times it out and scores the wait as failure -- indistinguishable in raw pass/fail from a genuine stale-state bug unless the window's fairness is itself audited.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Process-conformance blindness: rules stated in the visible spec (append-only history, ordering discipline, periodic liveness call) that only an end-state verifier checks, so an agent that violates the process but converges on a plausible final state is indistinguishable from a compliant one
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: Audit/compliance logging systems, distributed job schedulers requiring periodic heartbeats, event-sourced ledgers
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: process-trace vs. end-state verification gap (adjacent to partial-effect reconciliation / rollback-partial-success)
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: "an append-only journal requirement: an engine that deleted entries and recomputed still passed every final-state check" ... "a required periodic call: nothing required making the call, so an agent doing nothing satisfied every rule and passed" (DEFECT-TAXONOMY.md, class B1)
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: Agent must maintain a process invariant (never delete/rewrite history, call a heartbeat every N ticks, apply events in order) across a multi-step session; grading checks the full trace/audit log rather than only the final snapshot, so an agent that takes the end-state shortcut fails even though its final output looks correct.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Documented-vs-actual harness contract mismatch: the visible package promises a runtime guarantee (an object persists across sessions) that the actual harness silently violates, so agents that trust the documentation over the environment lose state
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: Stateful session/service-object runtimes, multi-turn agent harnesses with per-call object lifecycles
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: stale authority / contract drift between documented interface and live runtime
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: "a package stating that a facade object persists across sessions, while both the host and the runner constructed a new one per session. Submissions that trusted the published contract and scoped state to that object lost it at every boundary. The models that failed were the ones that believed the documentation." (DEFECT-TAXONOMY.md, class C1)
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: A task's public docs assert a persistence/identity guarantee about an object or handle across session boundaries; the actual test harness reconstructs it, so an agent that caches state against the documented contract instead of re-verifying at each boundary silently loses or duplicates work.

rawMechanismPool.mechanism: Browser/live-state replay: an action sequence valid against recorded/observed UI or backend state at capture time is replayed later against state that has since changed, and a naive agent executes the stale sequence instead of re-observing current state
rawMechanismPool.professionalDomain: Browser/UI automation agents, e-commerce or admin-panel workflow agents acting on live backends
rawMechanismPool.failureAxis: replay against changed state
rawMechanismPool.evidenceQuote: listed as a named but not-yet-built reallocation target: "reallocate build effort toward a different mechanism cluster such as model-alias rollout drift, delayed external receipts, browser/live-state replay, persistent prompt injection or hidden dependency discovery" (100K-TASK-PRODUCTION-STRATEGY.md, Section 4, Refinement: Lineage Kill And Reallocation)
rawMechanismPool.taskShapeSketch: An agent is given (or derives) a prior action/click/DOM sequence for a UI or API workflow, but between planning and execution the underlying state (stock level, IDs, page layout, auth token) has shifted; the family measures whether the agent re-observes current state before acting or blindly replays the stale plan.
